### Performance of the MINT sPLS-DA model - Implement ***zone-label shuffling*** with leave-one-group-out CV to generate a null distribution against which observed model performance can be benchmarked.

```{r MINT sPLS-DA model performance based on zone label shuffling, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Zone-label shuffling.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# ZONE-LABEL PERMUTATION TESTING FOR MINT sPLS-DA
# ============================================================

cat("=== PERMUTATION TESTING FOR MINT sPLS-DA ===\n\n")

# 1. SETUP
# ---------
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
n_permutations <- 999  # Standard in ecology

# Extract your tuned parameters from your existing model
ncomp <- final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$ncomp  # Should be 2
keepX <- final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$keepX  # Your tuned keepX values

# Extract data
X <- MAGs_MINT  # CLR-transformed abundances
Y <- pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing
study <- pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq_clr@sam_data$SECTOR_N_S

# 2. GET OBSERVED PERFORMANCE FROM YOUR EXISTING MODEL
# ----------------------------------------------------
# You already have this from your code!
# perf.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector contains the LOGOCV results

# Extract the correct observed accuracy
# From your code output, I see it's ~71% (0.71)
observed_error <- perf.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$global.error$BER[2]  # BER for 2 components
observed_accuracy <- 1 - observed_error

cat(sprintf("Observed accuracy from your tuned model: %.2f%%\n", observed_accuracy * 100))
cat(sprintf("(This should match the manuscript's 71%% accuracy)\n\n"))

# 3. PERMUTATION LOOP WITH PROGRESS TRACKING
# ------------------------------------------
cat("Running", n_permutations, "permutations...\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Initialize vector to store permuted accuracies
permuted_accuracies <- numeric(n_permutations)

# Set up progress tracking
start_time <- Sys.time()

# Run permutations in a loop (not parallel for better progress tracking)
for(i in 1:n_permutations) {
  
  # Print progress every 50 permutations
  if(i %% 50 == 0 || i == 1) {
    elapsed <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins")
    cat(sprintf("  Permutation %d/%d (%.1f%% complete) - Time elapsed: %.1f min\n", 
                i, n_permutations, (i/n_permutations)*100, elapsed))
  }
  
  # Shuffle zone labels WITHIN each sector
  # This preserves the sector structure while randomizing protection status
  Y_permuted <- Y
  for(sector in unique(study)) {
    sector_idx <- which(study == sector)
    Y_permuted[sector_idx] <- sample(Y[sector_idx])
  }
  
  # Run MINT sPLS-DA with permuted labels
  # Using same parameters as observed model
  perm_model <- tryCatch({
    mint.splsda(
      X = X,
      Y = Y_permuted,
      study = study,
      ncomp = ncomp,
      keepX = keepX,
      scale = TRUE
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("    Warning: Model failed for permutation", i, "-", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  # If model fails, skip this permutation
  if(is.null(perm_model)) {
    permuted_accuracies[i] <- NA
    next
  }
  
  # Evaluate with proper LOGOCV using perf() with Mfold
  # Note: For MINT objects, perf() automatically uses LOGOCV
  perm_perf <- tryCatch({
    perf(perm_model, 
         validation = "Mfold",  # For MINT, this does LOGOCV
         folds = 10,  # Number of folds within each study
         progressBar = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("    Warning: perf() failed for permutation", i, "-", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if(is.null(perm_perf)) {
    permuted_accuracies[i] <- NA
    next
  }
  
  # Extract BER for ncomp and convert to accuracy
  # Use the same number of components as your observed model
  perm_error <- perm_perf$global.error$BER[ncomp]
  permuted_accuracies[i] <- 1 - perm_error
}

# Calculate total time
total_time <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins")
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Permutations complete! Total time: %.1f minutes\n", total_time))

# Remove any NAs (failed permutations)
valid_permutations <- sum(!is.na(permuted_accuracies))
permuted_accuracies <- permuted_accuracies[!is.na(permuted_accuracies)]
cat(sprintf("Successful permutations: %d/%d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            valid_permutations, n_permutations, 
            (valid_permutations/n_permutations)*100))

# 4. CALCULATE P-VALUE
# --------------------
# Add 1 to both numerator and denominator for observed value
p_value <- (sum(permuted_accuracies >= observed_accuracy) + 1) / (length(permuted_accuracies) + 1)
cat(sprintf("\nP-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

# 5. VISUALIZATION
# ----------------

# Create data frame for plotting
perm_df <- data.frame(accuracy = permuted_accuracies)

# Calculate 95% confidence interval of null distribution
null_ci <- quantile(permuted_accuracies, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate max count for annotation positioning
hist_counts <- hist(permuted_accuracies, plot = FALSE)
max_count <- max(hist_counts$counts)

p <- ggplot(perm_df, aes(x = accuracy)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "gray70", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = observed_accuracy, 
             color = "red3", size = 1.5, linetype = "solid") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = null_ci, 
             color = "blue", size = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = observed_accuracy, y = max_count,
           label = sprintf("Observed: %.1f%%", observed_accuracy * 100),
           hjust = -0.1, color = "red3", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = null_ci[2], y = max_count * 0.9,
           label = "95% CI of null", hjust = -0.05, color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Classification Accuracy", 
       y = "Frequency",
       title = "Permutation Test: MINT sPLS-DA Classification Accuracy",
       subtitle = sprintf("Null distribution based on %d permutations\nObserved: %.1f%%, p = %.4f", 
                         length(permuted_accuracies), 
                         observed_accuracy * 100, 
                         p_value)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40"))

print(p)

# 6. SAVE RESULTS
# ---------------
ggsave("/home/marko-terzin/Documents/PhD/Thesis/Chapter_3_IMOS-MGD_MAGs/cleaned_code/Figure_2/output_pdf/permutation_test_results.pdf", p, width = 8, height = 5)

# Save numerical results
perm_results <- list(
  observed_accuracy = observed_accuracy,
  permuted_accuracies = permuted_accuracies,
  p_value = p_value,
  null_mean = mean(permuted_accuracies, na.rm = TRUE),
  null_sd = sd(permuted_accuracies, na.rm = TRUE),
  null_ci = null_ci,
  n_permutations = length(permuted_accuracies)
)

saveRDS(perm_results, "/home/marko-terzin/Documents/PhD/Thesis/Chapter_3_IMOS-MGD_MAGs/cleaned_code/Figure_2/output_stats/permutation_test_results.rds")

# 7. SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ---------------------
cat("\n=== PERMUTATION TEST SUMMARY ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Observed accuracy: %.2f%%\n", observed_accuracy * 100))
cat(sprintf("Null distribution mean: %.2f%% (sd = %.2f%%)\n", 
            mean(permuted_accuracies, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 
            sd(permuted_accuracies, na.rm = TRUE) * 100))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI of null: [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]\n", 
            null_ci[1] * 100, null_ci[2] * 100))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", p_value))

# 8. EFFECT SIZE
# --------------
cohens_d <- (observed_accuracy - mean(permuted_accuracies, na.rm = TRUE)) / 
            sd(permuted_accuracies, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("\nEffect size (Cohen's d): %.2f\n", cohens_d))

# 9. CREATE SUPPLEMENTARY TABLE
# ----------------------------

# Save all permutation results for supplementary
all_permutations_df <- data.frame(
  Permutation = 1:length(permuted_accuracies),
  Accuracy = round(permuted_accuracies * 100, 2)
)
write.csv(all_permutations_df, 
          "/home/marko-terzin/Documents/PhD/Thesis/Chapter_3_IMOS-MGD_MAGs/cleaned_code/Figure_2/output_stats/Supplementary_Table_All_Permutations.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nResults saved to:\n")
cat("  - permutation_test_results.pdf (figure)\n")
cat("  - permutation_test_results.rds (R object)\n")
cat("  - Supplementary_Table_All_Permutations.csv\n")
```

# Random Forest Validation of Reef Zoning Classification

To provide an independent, non-linear supervised framework alongside MINT sPLS-DA, we also implemented Random Forest classification. Using leave-one-sector-out cross-validation (identical to the MINT validation framework), we assessed whether microbial community composition can predict reef zoning status (NTMR vs. fished reefs). Model significance was evaluated through permutation testing (999 permutations with zone-label shuffling within sectors), generating a null distribution against which observed accuracy was benchmarked. Feature importance was quantified using Mean Decrease Accuracy, and the top 350 most important MAGs were compared with 350 MINT sPLS-DA indicators (component 1) to assess methodological concordance. Direction agreement between methods was evaluated for overlapping MAGs using Cohen's Kappa.

```{r MINT sPLS-DA and Random forest classification accuracy comparison, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Random Forest validation of reef zoning classification. (a) Leave-one-sector-out cross-validation accuracy across the seven GBR sectors. The red dashed line indicates mean RF accuracy (61.7%), the green dotted line shows MINT sPLS-DA accuracy (71%) for comparison. Error bars represent standard deviation across cross-validation folds. (b) Permutation test results showing the null distribution of classification accuracies from 999 permutations with zone labels shuffled within sectors. The red vertical line indicates observed RF accuracy (61.7%), blue dashed lines show the 95% confidence interval of the null distribution [38.8%, 56.1%]. p = 0.0020, confirming significant predictive performance. (c) Overlap between MINT sPLS-DA indicators (n = 350) and the top 350 most important RF features. Of the 350 MINT indicators, 140 (40.0%) appear in the RF top 350, representing the core microbial signal detectable by both linear discriminant and non-linear ensemble methods (Jaccard index = 0.250). (d) Top 20 most important RF features ranked by Mean Decrease Accuracy, with MAGs also selected by MINT highlighted in green. Taxonomic affiliation at genus level is shown where available.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# RANDOM FOREST CLASSIFICATION - PARALLELIZED VERSION
# ============================================================
# Using N-5 cores for optimal performance
# ============================================================

cat("\n\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 1: SETUP - Loading data and preparing for Random Forest\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

# 1. SETUP
# ---------
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
n_permutations <- 999  # Same as MINT permutation test

# Set up parallel processing
library(doParallel)
n_cores <- detectCores() - 5  # Use N-5 cores
cat(sprintf("Detected %d cores, using %d cores for parallel processing\n", 
            detectCores(), n_cores))

# Register parallel backend
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
registerDoParallel(cl)

# Export required packages to workers
clusterEvalQ(cl, {
  library(randomForest)
  library(foreach)
})

# Extract data (using same as MINT)
cat("Extracting microbial abundance data (CLR-transformed)...\n")
X_rf <- as.data.frame(MAGs_MINT)  # Features (CLR-transformed abundances)
cat(sprintf("  → Features matrix dimensions: %d samples × %d MAGs\n", nrow(X_rf), ncol(X_rf)))

cat("\nExtracting zone labels (Open/Closed to fishing)...\n")
Y_rf <- as.factor(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing)  # Labels
cat(sprintf("  → Class distribution:\n"))
cat(sprintf("    Closed (C): %d samples\n", sum(Y_rf == "C")))
cat(sprintf("    Open (O):   %d samples\n", sum(Y_rf == "O")))

cat("\nExtracting sector information for stratified CV...\n")
study_rf <- pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq_clr@sam_data$SECTOR_N_S
sectors <- unique(study_rf)
cat(sprintf("  → %d sectors: %s\n", length(sectors), paste(sectors, collapse = ", ")))

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 2: Leave-One-Sector-Out Cross-Validation (Full Model)\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

# 2. CROSS-VALIDATION SETUP
# --------------------------
n_sectors <- length(sectors)

cat("Training Random Forest models on 6 sectors, testing on the 7th...\n")
cat("(Using ALL 876 MAGs - matching MINT's full feature set)\n\n")

# Run CV folds in parallel
cat("Running cross-validation folds in parallel...\n")
start_time_cv <- Sys.time()

cv_results <- foreach(i = 1:n_sectors, .packages = c("randomForest")) %dopar% {
  
  # Split data
  test_idx <- which(study_rf == sectors[i])
  train_idx <- which(study_rf != sectors[i])
  
  X_train <- X_rf[train_idx, ]
  Y_train <- Y_rf[train_idx]
  X_test <- X_rf[test_idx, ]
  Y_test <- Y_rf[test_idx]
  
  # Train Random Forest with ALL features
  rf_model <- randomForest(
    x = X_train,
    y = Y_train,
    ntree = 1000,
    mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(X_train))),
    importance = TRUE,
    strata = Y_train,
    sampsize = rep(min(table(Y_train)), 2)
  )
  
  # Predict on test set
  rf_pred <- predict(rf_model, X_test)
  
  # Calculate accuracy
  fold_accuracy <- mean(rf_pred == Y_test)
  
  # Return results
  list(
    accuracy = fold_accuracy,
    importance = importance(rf_model),
    sector = as.character(sectors[i])
  )
}

# Extract results
rf_cv_accuracy <- sapply(cv_results, function(x) x$accuracy)
rf_importance_list <- lapply(cv_results, function(x) x$importance)

cv_time <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_time_cv, units = "mins")
cat(sprintf("\nCross-validation completed in %.1f minutes\n", cv_time))

# Overall CV performance
rf_mean_accuracy <- mean(rf_cv_accuracy)
rf_sd_accuracy <- sd(rf_cv_accuracy)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 2 COMPLETE: Cross-Validation Results (Full Model)\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean CV accuracy: %.2f%% (±%.2f%%)\n", 
            rf_mean_accuracy * 100, rf_sd_accuracy * 100))
cat(sprintf("Range: [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]\n", 
            min(rf_cv_accuracy) * 100, max(rf_cv_accuracy) * 100))
cat(sprintf("\nComparison with MINT sPLS-DA: %.2f%%\n", 71.0))

# Print per-sector accuracies
cat("\nPer-sector accuracies:\n")
for(i in 1:n_sectors) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %.2f%%\n", sectors[i], rf_cv_accuracy[i] * 100))
}

cat("\n\n============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 3: Permutation Testing (Zone-label shuffling)\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

# 3. PERMUTATION TESTING (parallelized)
# --------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("Running %d permutations to generate null distribution...\n", n_permutations))
cat(sprintf("Using %d cores in parallel\n", n_cores))
cat("(Shuffling zone labels WITHIN each sector to preserve spatial structure)\n\n")

# Export data to workers
clusterExport(cl, c("X_rf", "Y_rf", "study_rf", "sectors", "n_sectors"))

# Run permutations in parallel with progress tracking
start_time_perm <- Sys.time()

perm_accuracies <- foreach(p = 1:n_permutations, 
                           .combine = c,
                           .packages = c("randomForest")) %dopar% {
  
  # Shuffle labels WITHIN each sector
  Y_perm <- Y_rf
  for(sector in sectors) {
    sector_idx <- which(study_rf == sector)
    Y_perm[sector_idx] <- sample(Y_rf[sector_idx])
  }
  
  # Run CV with permuted labels
  perm_fold_acc <- numeric(n_sectors)
  
  for(i in 1:n_sectors) {
    test_idx <- which(study_rf == sectors[i])
    train_idx <- which(study_rf != sectors[i])
    
    rf_perm <- randomForest(
      x = X_rf[train_idx, ],
      y = Y_perm[train_idx],
      ntree = 500,  # Fewer trees for speed
      mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(X_rf))),
      importance = FALSE
    )
    
    pred_perm <- predict(rf_perm, X_rf[test_idx, ])
    perm_fold_acc[i] <- mean(pred_perm == Y_perm[test_idx])
  }
  
  mean(perm_fold_acc)
}

# Progress tracking in main thread
for(p in seq(100, n_permutations, 100)) {
  elapsed <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_time_perm, units = "mins")
  cat(sprintf("  Progress: %d/%d permutations (%.1f%%) - Time: %.1f min\n", 
              p, n_permutations, (p/n_permutations)*100, elapsed))
}

total_time_perm <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_time_perm, units = "mins")
cat(sprintf("\nPermutations complete! Total time: %.1f minutes\n", total_time_perm))

# Calculate p-value
rf_p_value <- (sum(perm_accuracies >= rf_mean_accuracy) + 1) / (n_permutations + 1)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 3 COMPLETE: Permutation Test Results\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Observed accuracy: %.2f%%\n", rf_mean_accuracy * 100))
cat(sprintf("Null distribution mean: %.2f%%\n", mean(perm_accuracies) * 100))
cat(sprintf("Null distribution SD: %.2f%%\n", sd(perm_accuracies) * 100))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI of null: [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]\n", 
            quantile(perm_accuracies, 0.025) * 100,
            quantile(perm_accuracies, 0.975) * 100))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", rf_p_value))

cat("\n\n============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 4: Feature Selection - Identifying Top RF Indicators\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

# 4. AVERAGE FEATURE IMPORTANCE
# ------------------------------
cat("Averaging feature importance across all CV folds...\n")
# Sum all importance matrices then divide
avg_importance <- Reduce(`+`, rf_importance_list) / length(rf_importance_list)

# Get ALL features ranked by importance
importance_df <- data.frame(
  MAG = rownames(avg_importance),
  MeanDecreaseAccuracy = avg_importance[, "MeanDecreaseAccuracy"],
  MeanDecreaseGini = avg_importance[, "MeanDecreaseGini"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseAccuracy))

cat(sprintf("Total features ranked: %d\n", nrow(importance_df)))

# Verify sorting BEFORE adding taxonomy
cat("\nTop 10 MAGs by importance (BEFORE adding taxonomy):\n")
print(head(importance_df[, c("MAG", "MeanDecreaseAccuracy")], 10))

# Add taxonomy WITHOUT MERGE (use match() to preserve order)
cat("\nAdding taxonomic information while preserving order...\n")
tax_info <- as.data.frame(tax_table(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq))

# Create new columns in importance_df by matching MAG names
importance_df$Domain <- tax_info$Domain[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]
importance_df$Phylum <- tax_info$Phylum[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]
importance_df$Class <- tax_info$Class[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]
importance_df$Order <- tax_info$Order[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]
importance_df$Family <- tax_info$Family[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]
importance_df$Genus <- tax_info$Genus[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]
importance_df$Species <- tax_info$Species[match(importance_df$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]

# Verify sorting AFTER adding taxonomy
cat("\nTop 10 MAGs by importance (AFTER adding taxonomy - order preserved):\n")
print(head(importance_df[, c("MAG", "MeanDecreaseAccuracy", "Genus")], 10))

# Find the importance score at position 350
importance_350th <- importance_df$MeanDecreaseAccuracy[350]
cat(sprintf("\nImportance score at position 350: %.4f\n", importance_350th))

# Select all MAGs with importance score >= the 350th highest score
# This ensures we get exactly the top 350 most important features
rf_top_350 <- importance_df[importance_df$MeanDecreaseAccuracy >= importance_350th, ]

# In case of ties at the cutoff, we might get slightly more than 350
# If that happens, we take the first 350 to be exact
if(nrow(rf_top_350) > 350) {
  cat(sprintf("\nNote: %d MAGs at cutoff (ties), taking first 350\n", nrow(rf_top_350)))
  rf_top_350 <- rf_top_350[1:350, ]
} else {
  cat(sprintf("\nExactly %d MAGs selected\n", nrow(rf_top_350)))
}

cat(sprintf("\nSelected top %d RF features\n", nrow(rf_top_350)))
cat(sprintf("Importance score range in top 350: %.4f to %.4f\n", 
            min(rf_top_350$MeanDecreaseAccuracy),
            max(rf_top_350$MeanDecreaseAccuracy)))

cat("\nTop 10 most important MAGs according to Random Forest:\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------\n")
for(j in 1:10) {
  genus <- ifelse(!is.na(rf_top_350$Genus[j]) & rf_top_350$Genus[j] != "",
                  rf_top_350$Genus[j],
                  "Unknown")
  cat(sprintf("%2d. %s (Genus: %s) - MDA: %.2f\n", 
              j, substr(rf_top_350$MAG[j], 1, 20), 
              genus, rf_top_350$MeanDecreaseAccuracy[j]))
}

cat("\n\n============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 5: Comparison with MINT sPLS-DA Indicators\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

# 5. COMPARE WITH MINT INDICATORS
# --------------------------------
cat("Loading MINT sPLS-DA indicators (component 1)...\n")
mint_indicators <- selectVar(final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector, comp = 1)$name
cat(sprintf("MINT selected %d indicator MAGs\n", length(mint_indicators)))

# Overlap between top 350 RF and MINT indicators
rf_mint_overlap <- intersect(rf_top_350$MAG, mint_indicators)

cat("\nOverlap Analysis (FAIR COMPARISON: Top 350 RF vs 350 MINT):\n")
cat("-----------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat(sprintf("MINT indicators:                    %3d MAGs\n", length(mint_indicators)))
cat(sprintf("Top 350 RF important features:      %3d MAGs\n", nrow(rf_top_350)))
cat(sprintf("Overlap (in both sets):             %3d MAGs\n", length(rf_mint_overlap)))
cat(sprintf("Percentage of MINT in top 350 RF:   %.1f%%\n", 
            length(rf_mint_overlap)/350 * 100))
cat(sprintf("Percentage of RF in MINT:           %.1f%%\n", 
            length(rf_mint_overlap)/350 * 100))

# Check if top RF features are also in MINT
cat("\nTop 10 RF features - are they MINT indicators?\n")
cat("--------------------------------------------\n")
for(j in 1:10) {
  in_mint <- ifelse(rf_top_350$MAG[j] %in% mint_indicators, "✓ YES", "✗ no")
  cat(sprintf("%2d. %s... [%s]\n", j, substr(rf_top_350$MAG[j], 1, 30), in_mint))
}

# Jaccard similarity index
jaccard <- length(rf_mint_overlap) / (length(mint_indicators) + length(rf_top_350$MAG) - length(rf_mint_overlap))
cat(sprintf("\nJaccard similarity index: %.3f\n", jaccard))
cat("(0 = no overlap, 1 = perfect overlap)\n")

# Check overlap at different thresholds to see if it's stable
cat("\n=== OVERLAP AT DIFFERENT THRESHOLDS ===\n")
thresholds <- c(100, 200, 300, 350, 400, 500)
for(t in thresholds) {
  t_score <- importance_df$MeanDecreaseAccuracy[t]
  t_mags <- importance_df[importance_df$MeanDecreaseAccuracy >= t_score, ]
  if(nrow(t_mags) > t) t_mags <- t_mags[1:t, ]
  t_overlap <- intersect(t_mags$MAG, mint_indicators)
  cat(sprintf("Top %d: %d overlap (%.1f%%)\n", 
              t, length(t_overlap), length(t_overlap)/t*100))
}

cat("\n\n============================================================\n")
cat("RANDOM FOREST VALIDATION COMPLETE\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("RF Accuracy (full model):  %.2f%% | MINT Accuracy: 71%%\n", rf_mean_accuracy * 100))
cat(sprintf("RF p-value:                %.4f\n", rf_p_value))
cat(sprintf("Feature overlap:           %d MAGs (%.1f%% of MINT indicators)\n", 
            length(rf_mint_overlap), 
            length(rf_mint_overlap)/350 * 100))

if(rf_p_value < 0.001) {
  cat("\n✓ RF model is HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT (p < 0.001)\n")
} else if(rf_p_value < 0.01) {
  cat("\n✓ RF model is VERY SIGNIFICANT (p < 0.01)\n")
} else if(rf_p_value < 0.05) {
  cat("\n✓ RF model is SIGNIFICANT (p < 0.05)\n")
} else {
  cat("\n✗ RF model is NOT SIGNIFICANT\n")
}

if(length(rf_mint_overlap) >= 175) {
  cat("✓ STRONG feature overlap (>50% of MINT indicators in RF top 350)\n")
} else if(length(rf_mint_overlap) >= 105) {
  cat("✓ MODERATE feature overlap (>30% of MINT indicators in RF top 350)\n")
} else {
  cat("! LOW feature overlap - methods may capture different signals\n")
}

# 6. VISUALIZATION (run in main thread)
# -------------------------------------
cat("\n\nGenerating visualization plots...\n")

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# Plot 1: CV accuracy by sector
sector_acc_df <- data.frame(
  Sector = sectors,
  Accuracy = rf_cv_accuracy * 100
)

p1 <- ggplot(sector_acc_df, aes(x = reorder(Sector, Accuracy), y = Accuracy)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = rf_mean_accuracy * 100, 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red3", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 71, 
             linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgreen", size = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = rf_mean_accuracy * 100 + 2, 
           label = sprintf("RF mean: %.1f%%", rf_mean_accuracy * 100),
           hjust = 0, color = "red3", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 73, 
           label = "MINT: 71%", hjust = 0, color = "darkgreen", size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Sector", y = "Classification Accuracy (%)",
       title = "RF Performance by Sector",
       subtitle = sprintf("Mean: %.1f%% (±%.1f%%)", 
                         rf_mean_accuracy * 100, rf_sd_accuracy * 100)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Plot 2: Permutation test
perm_df <- data.frame(accuracy = perm_accuracies * 100)
null_ci <- quantile(perm_accuracies * 100, c(0.025, 0.975))

p2 <- ggplot(perm_df, aes(x = accuracy)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "gray70", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = rf_mean_accuracy * 100, 
             color = "red3", size = 1.5, linetype = "solid") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = null_ci, 
             color = "blue", size = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = rf_mean_accuracy * 100, y = max(hist(perm_accuracies*100, plot=FALSE)$counts),
           label = sprintf("Observed: %.1f%%", rf_mean_accuracy * 100),
           hjust = -0.1, color = "red3", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "Classification Accuracy (%)", y = "Frequency",
       title = "RF Permutation Test",
       subtitle = sprintf("Null mean: %.1f%%, p = %.4f", 
                         mean(perm_accuracies) * 100, rf_p_value)) +
  theme_minimal()

# Plot 3: RF vs MINT overlap
overlap_df <- data.frame(
  Method = c("MINT only", "Both", "RF only"),
  Count = c(
    length(setdiff(mint_indicators, rf_top_350$MAG)),
    length(rf_mint_overlap),
    length(setdiff(rf_top_350$MAG, mint_indicators))
  )
)

p3 <- ggplot(overlap_df, aes(x = Method, y = Count, fill = Method)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MINT only" = "#E69F00", 
                               "Both" = "#2E8B57",
                               "RF only" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of MAGs",
       title = "Feature Overlap (Top 350 RF vs 350 MINT)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Jaccard index = %.3f", jaccard)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot 4: Top RF features with taxonomy
top_20_plot <- head(rf_top_350, 20)
top_20_plot$Label <- ifelse(!is.na(top_20_plot$Genus) & top_20_plot$Genus != "",
                            paste0(top_20_plot$Genus, " (", 
                                   substr(top_20_plot$MAG, 1, 6), ")"),
                            substr(top_20_plot$MAG, 1, 15))
top_20_plot$MINT_Indicator <- ifelse(top_20_plot$MAG %in% mint_indicators, 
                                     "Yes", "No")

p4 <- ggplot(top_20_plot, aes(x = reorder(Label, MeanDecreaseAccuracy), 
                              y = MeanDecreaseAccuracy,
                              fill = MINT_Indicator)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#2E8B57", "No" = "gray60")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean Decrease Accuracy",
       title = "Top 20 RF Important Features",
       subtitle = "Green = also selected by MINT") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Combine plots
combined_plot <- (p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Random Forest Validation of Reef Zoning Classification",
    subtitle = sprintf("Independent non-linear model: %.1f%% accuracy (p = %.4f), %.1f%% overlap with MINT", 
                      rf_mean_accuracy * 100, rf_p_value,
                      length(rf_mint_overlap)/350 * 100),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40", size = 11))
  )

print(combined_plot)

# Save results
cat("\nSaving results...\n")
ggsave("random_forest_validation.pdf", combined_plot, width = 14, height = 10)

# Stop cluster
stopCluster(cl)

# Save numerical results
rf_results <- list(
  cv_accuracy = rf_cv_accuracy,
  mean_accuracy = rf_mean_accuracy,
  sd_accuracy = rf_sd_accuracy,
  perm_accuracies = perm_accuracies,
  p_value = rf_p_value,
  importance = importance_df,
  top_350 = rf_top_350,
  mint_overlap = rf_mint_overlap,
  jaccard = jaccard,
  sectors = sectors
)

saveRDS(rf_results, "random_forest_results.rds")
write.csv(rf_top_350, "RF_top_350_indicators.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("✓ Results saved to:\n")
cat("  - random_forest_validation.pdf\n")
cat("  - random_forest_results.rds\n")
cat("  - RF_top_350_indicators.csv\n")
```

```{r MINT sPLS-DA and Random forest indicator direction comparison, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Direction agreement between MINT sPLS-DA and Random Forest for overlapping indicator MAGs. (a) Confusion matrix showing perfect agreement in enrichment direction assignment between methods. All 78 NTMR-enriched and 62 Fished-enriched MAGs identified by both approaches show identical direction (Cohen's Kappa = 1.000, p < 0.001), confirming that the core microbial signal is robust across fundamentally different modelling frameworks. (b) Scatter plot of MINT loadings vs. RF difference (NTMR - Fished CLR mean) for the 140 overlapping MAGs. Points in the upper-right and lower-left quadrants indicate perfect directional concordance (positive = NTMR-enriched, negative = Fished-enriched). (c) Family-level taxonomic distribution of the 140 overlapping MAGs, separated by enrichment direction. NTMR-enriched MAGs (green) are dominated by oligotrophic taxa (Pelagibacteraceae, SAR86, UBA817), while Fished-enriched MAGs (blue) are dominated by copiotrophic taxa (Flavobacteriaceae, UA16, Schleiferiaceae), consistent with the ecological patterns observed in the full MINT analysis.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# STEP 6: Direction Agreement Analysis - MINT vs Random Forest
# ============================================================

cat("\n\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("STEP 6: Direction Agreement Analysis - MINT vs Random Forest\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

# 1. Get enrichment direction from MINT sPLS-DA
# ---------------------------------------------
cat("Extracting enrichment direction from MINT sPLS-DA...\n")

# Get loadings from MINT (component 1)
mint_loadings <- selectVar(final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector, comp = 1)

# Create MINT direction dataframe
mint_direction <- data.frame(
  MAG = mint_loadings$name,
  MINT_Loading = mint_loadings$value,
  MINT_Direction = ifelse(mint_loadings$value < 0, "Fished-enriched", "NTMR-enriched"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cat(sprintf("  → MINT indicators: %d total\n", nrow(mint_direction)))
cat(sprintf("  → NTMR-enriched: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(mint_direction$value.var.1 == "NTMR-enriched"),
            sum(mint_direction$value.var.1 == "NTMR-enriched")/nrow(mint_direction)*100))
cat(sprintf("  → Fished-enriched: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(mint_direction$value.var.1 == "Fished-enriched"),
            sum(mint_direction$value.var.1 == "Fished-enriched")/nrow(mint_direction)*100))

# 2. Get enrichment direction from Random Forest
# ----------------------------------------------
cat("\nExtracting enrichment direction from Random Forest...\n")

# Get raw abundance data (before CLR)
raw_abundances <- as.matrix(pMAGs_95ANI)  # Your raw count matrix

# Get zone labels
zone_labels <- pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing

# Create a simpler approach: use the CLR-transformed data that's already in your MINT object
# This avoids issues with zeros and pseudocounts
cat("Using CLR-transformed abundances for direction calculation...\n")
clr_abundances <- as.matrix(MAGs_MINT)  # This has samples as rows, MAGs as columns
# Transpose to match raw_abundances format (MAGs as rows)
clr_abundances <- t(clr_abundances)

# Calculate mean CLR abundance in each zone for top 350 RF features
rf_direction_list <- list()
success_count <- 0
error_count <- 0

for(i in 1:nrow(rf_top_350)) {
  mag <- rf_top_350$MAG[i]
  
  # Print progress every 50 MAGs
  if(i %% 50 == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  Processing MAG %d/%d\n", i, nrow(rf_top_350)))
  }
  
  # Check if MAG exists in the abundance matrix
  if(mag %in% rownames(clr_abundances)) {
    
    # Get abundances for this MAG
    mag_abund <- clr_abundances[mag, ]
    
    # Get indices for each zone
    closed_idx <- which(zone_labels == "C")
    open_idx <- which(zone_labels == "O")
    
    # Calculate mean CLR abundance in each zone
    mean_closed <- mean(mag_abund[closed_idx], na.rm = TRUE)
    mean_open <- mean(mag_abund[open_idx], na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Check if means are valid
    if(is.finite(mean_closed) && is.finite(mean_open)) {
      
      # Calculate difference (Closed - Open)
      # Positive = higher in NTMR, Negative = higher in Fished
      diff <- mean_closed - mean_open
      
      # Determine direction
      if(diff > 0) {
        direction <- "NTMR-enriched"
      } else if(diff < 0) {
        direction <- "Fished-enriched"
      } else {
        direction <- "Equal"
      }
      
      rf_direction_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
        MAG = mag,
        RF_Diff = diff,
        RF_Direction = direction,
        Mean_NTMR_CLR = mean_closed,
        Mean_Fished_CLR = mean_open,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      success_count <- success_count + 1
    } else {
      error_count <- error_count + 1
    }
  } else {
    error_count <- error_count + 1
  }
}

# Combine results, removing NULL entries
rf_direction_list <- rf_direction_list[!sapply(rf_direction_list, is.null)]
rf_direction <- do.call(rbind, rf_direction_list)

cat(sprintf("\n  → Successfully processed: %d MAGs\n", nrow(rf_direction)))
cat(sprintf("  → Skipped/errors: %d MAGs\n", error_count))
cat(sprintf("  → NTMR-enriched: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(rf_direction$RF_Direction == "NTMR-enriched", na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(rf_direction$RF_Direction == "NTMR-enriched", na.rm = TRUE)/nrow(rf_direction)*100))
cat(sprintf("  → Fished-enriched: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(rf_direction$RF_Direction == "Fished-enriched", na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(rf_direction$RF_Direction == "Fished-enriched", na.rm = TRUE)/nrow(rf_direction)*100))
cat(sprintf("  → Equal: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(rf_direction$RF_Direction == "Equal", na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(rf_direction$RF_Direction == "Equal", na.rm = TRUE)/nrow(rf_direction)*100))

# 3. Combine direction information for overlapping MAGs
# -----------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n============================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Direction Agreement for Overlapping MAGs\n"))
cat("============================================================\n")

# Get overlapping MAGs
overlap_mags <- intersect(rf_top_350$MAG, mint_direction$MAG)
cat(sprintf("Overlapping MAGs: %d\n", length(overlap_mags)))

# Merge direction information
direction_comparison <- merge(
  mint_direction[mint_direction$MAG %in% overlap_mags, ],
  rf_direction[rf_direction$MAG %in% overlap_mags, ],
  by = "MAG"
)

# Add taxonomy
tax_info <- as.data.frame(tax_table(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq))
direction_comparison <- merge(
  direction_comparison,
  tax_info,
  by.x = "MAG",
  by.y = "row.names",
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Determine agreement
direction_comparison$Agreement <- ifelse(
  direction_comparison$value.var.1 == direction_comparison$RF_Direction,
  "Agree", "Disagree"
)

# 4. Calculate agreement statistics
# ---------------------------------
cat("\nAGREEMENT STATISTICS:\n")
cat("--------------------\n")
cat(sprintf("Total overlapping MAGs: %d\n", nrow(direction_comparison)))
cat(sprintf("MAGs with AGREED direction: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(direction_comparison$Agreement == "Agree"),
            sum(direction_comparison$Agreement == "Agree")/nrow(direction_comparison)*100))
cat(sprintf("MAGs with DISAGREED direction: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
            sum(direction_comparison$Agreement == "Disagree"),
            sum(direction_comparison$Agreement == "Disagree")/nrow(direction_comparison)*100))

# By enrichment category
cat("\nAGREEMENT BY ENRICHMENT DIRECTION:\n")
cat("----------------------------------\n")

# NTMR-enriched MAGs
ntmr_overlap <- direction_comparison[direction_comparison$value.var.1 == "NTMR-enriched", ]
if(nrow(ntmr_overlap) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("NTMR-enriched MAGs: %d total\n", nrow(ntmr_overlap)))
  cat(sprintf("  → Agreed: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              sum(ntmr_overlap$Agreement == "Agree"),
              sum(ntmr_overlap$Agreement == "Agree")/nrow(ntmr_overlap)*100))
  cat(sprintf("  → Disagreed: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              sum(ntmr_overlap$Agreement == "Disagree"),
              sum(ntmr_overlap$Agreement == "Disagree")/nrow(ntmr_overlap)*100))
}

# Fished-enriched MAGs
fished_overlap <- direction_comparison[direction_comparison$value.var.1 == "Fished-enriched", ]
if(nrow(fished_overlap) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("\nFished-enriched MAGs: %d total\n", nrow(fished_overlap)))
  cat(sprintf("  → Agreed: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              sum(fished_overlap$Agreement == "Agree"),
              sum(fished_overlap$Agreement == "Agree")/nrow(fished_overlap)*100))
  cat(sprintf("  → Disagreed: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              sum(fished_overlap$Agreement == "Disagree"),
              sum(fished_overlap$Agreement == "Disagree")/nrow(fished_overlap)*100))
}

# 5. Create visualization
# -----------------------
cat("\n\nGenerating direction agreement plots...\n")

# Plot 1: Confusion matrix of direction agreement
agreement_matrix <- data.frame(
  MINT_Direction = c("NTMR-enriched", "NTMR-enriched", "Fished-enriched", "Fished-enriched"),
  RF_Direction = c("NTMR-enriched", "Fished-enriched", "NTMR-enriched", "Fished-enriched"),
  Count = c(
    sum(direction_comparison$value.var.1 == "NTMR-enriched" & 
        direction_comparison$RF_Direction == "NTMR-enriched"),
    sum(direction_comparison$value.var.1 == "NTMR-enriched" & 
        direction_comparison$RF_Direction == "Fished-enriched"),
    sum(direction_comparison$value.var.1 == "Fished-enriched" & 
        direction_comparison$RF_Direction == "NTMR-enriched"),
    sum(direction_comparison$value.var.1 == "Fished-enriched" & 
        direction_comparison$RF_Direction == "Fished-enriched")
  )
)

# Remove zero rows for cleaner plot
agreement_matrix <- agreement_matrix[agreement_matrix$Count > 0, ]

p1 <- ggplot(agreement_matrix, aes(x = MINT_Direction, y = RF_Direction, fill = Count)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black", size = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), size = 6, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "steelblue4", high = "seagreen3") +
  labs(x = "MINT sPLS-DA Direction", y = "Random Forest Direction",
       title = "Direction Agreement Matrix",
       subtitle = sprintf("Overall agreement: %.1f%%", 
                         sum(direction_comparison$Agreement == "Agree")/nrow(direction_comparison)*100)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Plot 2: Scatter plot of MINT loadings vs RF difference
p2 <- ggplot(direction_comparison, aes(x = value.var, y = RF_Diff, color = Agreement)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Agree" = "plum4", "Disagree" = "#D95F02")) +
  labs(x = "MINT Loading (component 1)", 
       y = "RF Difference (NTMR - Fished CLR mean)",
       title = "Direction Consistency",
       subtitle = "Positive = NTMR-enriched, Negative = Fished-enriched") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

# Plot 3: Taxonomic distribution of overlapping MAGs by enrichment direction
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(nrow(direction_comparison) > 0) {
  
  # Clean up Family names (remove "f__" prefix for readability)
  direction_comparison$Family_clean <- gsub("^f__", "", direction_comparison$Family)
  direction_comparison$Family_clean <- ifelse(is.na(direction_comparison$Family_clean) | 
                                              direction_comparison$Family_clean == "",
                                             "Unknown", direction_comparison$Family_clean)
  
  # Summarize counts by Family and Enrichment Direction (using MINT direction since they agree)
  family_enrichment_counts <- direction_comparison %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Family_clean, value.var.1) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(Count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(Count))
  
  # Get top 15 families overall (for display)
  top_families <- family_enrichment_counts %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Family_clean) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(Total = sum(Count)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(Total)) %>%
    head(15) %>%
    pull(Family_clean)
  
  # Filter to top families
  family_enrichment_top <- family_enrichment_counts %>%
    dplyr::filter(Family_clean %in% top_families)
  
  # Order families by total count
  family_order <- family_enrichment_top %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Family_clean) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(Total = sum(Count)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(Total)) %>%
    pull(Family_clean)
  
  family_enrichment_top$Family_clean <- factor(family_enrichment_top$Family_clean, 
                                               levels = rev(family_order))
  
  # Create the plot
  p3 <- ggplot(family_enrichment_top, 
               aes(x = Family_clean, y = Count, fill = value.var.1)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Count, group = value.var.1),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
              hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "NTMR-enriched" = "seagreen3",
        "Fished-enriched" = "steelblue4"
      ),
      name = "Enrichment direction"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Family-level distribution of overlapping indicators",
      subtitle = paste("Top 15 families among", nrow(direction_comparison), 
                      "MAGs identified by both MINT and Random Forest"),
      x = "Family", 
      y = "Number of MAGs"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40", size = 11),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
    ) +
    ylim(0, max(family_enrichment_top$Count) * 1.2)
  
  # Also create a summary table
  cat("\n\n=== TOP FAMILIES BY ENRICHMENT DIRECTION ===\n")
  print(family_enrichment_top)
  
} else {
  p3 <- ggplot() + 
    annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "No overlapping MAGs found", size = 5) + 
    theme_void()
}

# Update the combined plot - now just p1 + p2 + p3
combined_dir_plot <- p1 + p2 + p3 +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Method Agreement: MINT sPLS-DA vs Random Forest",
    subtitle = sprintf("%d overlapping MAGs | %.1f%% direction agreement", 
                      nrow(direction_comparison),
                      sum(direction_comparison$Agreement == "Agree")/nrow(direction_comparison)*100),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40", size = 12))
  ) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3)  # Three panels side by side

# Save
ggsave("direction_agreement_summary.pdf", combined_dir_plot, width = 18, height = 8)

cat("\n✓ Direction agreement analysis complete!\n")
cat("  Results saved to: direction_agreement_summary.pdf\n")

# Cohen's Kappa for inter-method agreement
if(require(irr, quietly = TRUE)) {
  kappa_result <- kappa2(data.frame(
    MINT = as.factor(direction_comparison$value.var.1),
    RF = as.factor(direction_comparison$RF_Direction)
  ))
  
  cat(sprintf("\nCohen's Kappa: %.3f\n", kappa_result$value))
  cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", kappa_result$p.value))
  
  if(kappa_result$value > 0.8) {
    cat("Interpretation: Almost perfect agreement\n")
  } else if(kappa_result$value > 0.6) {
    cat("Interpretation: Substantial agreement\n")
  } else if(kappa_result$value > 0.4) {
    cat("Interpretation: Moderate agreement\n")
  } else if(kappa_result$value > 0.2) {
    cat("Interpretation: Fair agreement\n")
  } else {
    cat("Interpretation: Slight agreement\n")
  }
}

cat("\n✓ Direction agreement analysis complete!\n")
cat("  Results saved to:\n")
cat("  - direction_agreement_analysis_all_taxa.pdf (full figure with all MAGs)\n")
cat("  - direction_agreement_summary.pdf (summary plots only)\n")
cat("  - MINT_RF_direction_comparison_all.csv\n")
```


# Validating indicator microbes

## ***Presence/Absence*** Validation:

To complement the abundance-based indicator analysis, we will examine the presence/absence patterns of the identified indicator MAGs across all samples. We hypothesise that most, if not all, of these taxa are present in both fished and NTMR zones. A significant difference in their detection frequency (not just abundance) would further support their role as robust indicators, independent of genome size effects. Conversely, if differential presence is observed, it would point to an even stronger, fundamental ecological difference.

```{r MINT sPLS-DA indicators presence absence across all sites, fig.height=24, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Near-universal presence of MINT sPLS-DA indicator pMAGs across the Great Barrier Reef validates abundance-based ecological signals. (A) Distribution of presence percentages for the 350 MINT sPLS-DA-selected indicator MAGs across 190 seawater samples. The dashed red line indicates complete presence (100% of samples), with 317 MAGs (90.6%) detected in every sample. (B) Presence/absence heatmap showing all 350 indicator MAGs (y-axis, ordered by presence frequency) across all reef sites (x-axis), separated into NTMR (closed) and fished (open) zones. White tiles indicate absence, plum4 tiles indicate presence. (C) Detailed view of the 33 indicator MAGs with <100% presence across sites, annotated with taxonomic classification (genus or family) and presence percentage. The widespread presence of indicator MAGs across all sites demonstrates that observed abundance differences reflect genuine ecological variation rather than detection artifacts or genome size bias.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# First, let's identify which MAGs were selected by MINT sPLS-DA
mint_indicators <- selectVar(final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector, comp = 1)$name
cat("Number of indicator MAGs from MINT sPLS-DA:", length(mint_indicators), "\n")

# Get the original count matrix (before CLR transformation)
original_counts <- pMAGs_95ANI  # This should have raw counts with zeros
dim(original_counts)

# Subset to only the indicator MAGs
indicator_counts <- original_counts[rownames(original_counts) %in% mint_indicators, ]
dim(indicator_counts)

# Calculate presence/absence (1 = present, 0 = absent)
presence_absence <- indicator_counts
presence_absence[presence_absence > 0] <- 1

# Summarize presence across all samples
presence_summary <- data.frame(
  MAG = rownames(presence_absence),
  Total_Samples = ncol(presence_absence),
  Present_in = rowSums(presence_absence),
  Present_Percent = (rowSums(presence_absence) / ncol(presence_absence)) * 100,
  Mean_Abundance = rowMeans(original_counts[rownames(presence_absence), ]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Add taxonomy information
tax_info <- as.data.frame(tax_table(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq))
presence_summary <- cbind(presence_summary, 
                          tax_info[presence_summary$MAG, ])

# Display summary
cat("\n=== PRESENCE/ABSENCE SUMMARY OF INDICATOR MAGS ===\n")
cat("Total samples:", ncol(presence_absence), "\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs present in all samples:", sum(presence_summary$Present_Percent == 100), "\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs present in >95% of samples:", sum(presence_summary$Present_Percent > 95), "\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs present in >90% of samples:", sum(presence_summary$Present_Percent > 90), "\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs present in >75% of samples:", sum(presence_summary$Present_Percent > 75), "\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs present in <50% of samples:", sum(presence_summary$Present_Percent < 50), "\n")

# View the least common indicators
cat("\n=== LEAST COMMON INDICATOR MAGS (by presence) ===\n")
least_common <- presence_summary[order(presence_summary$Present_Percent), ]
print(head(least_common[, c("MAG", "Class", "Order", "Present_Percent", "Mean_Abundance")], 10))

# ============================================================
# Getting the stats
# ============================================================

# Get metadata for grouping
metadata_for_pa <- as.data.frame(sample_data(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq_clr)) %>% 
  as.matrix() %>% 
  as.data.frame()

# Calculate presence/absence separately for Open and Closed sites
open_samples <- metadata_for_pa$Sample_ID[metadata_for_pa$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing == "O"]
closed_samples <- metadata_for_pa$Sample_ID[metadata_for_pa$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing == "C"]

presence_open <- presence_absence[, colnames(presence_absence) %in% open_samples]
presence_closed <- presence_absence[, colnames(presence_absence) %in% closed_samples]

# Compare presence between zones
presence_comparison <- data.frame(
  MAG = rownames(presence_absence),
  Present_Open = rowSums(presence_open),
  Present_Closed = rowSums(presence_closed),
  Total_Open = ncol(presence_open),
  Total_Closed = ncol(presence_closed),
  Percent_Open = (rowSums(presence_open) / ncol(presence_open)) * 100,
  Percent_Closed = (rowSums(presence_closed) / ncol(presence_closed)) * 100,
  Presence_Difference = abs((rowSums(presence_open) / ncol(presence_open)) - 
                           (rowSums(presence_closed) / ncol(presence_closed))) * 100
)

# Add taxonomy
presence_comparison <- cbind(presence_comparison, 
                            tax_info[presence_comparison$MAG, ])

# Summary
cat("\n=== PRESENCE COMPARISON BETWEEN ZONES ===\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs significantly different in presence (FDR < 0.05):", 
    sum(presence_comparison$FDR < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Indicator MAGs with >20% presence difference:", 
    sum(presence_comparison$Presence_Difference > 20), "\n")
cat("Mean presence difference:", 
    mean(presence_comparison$Presence_Difference, na.rm = TRUE), "%\n")

# ============================================================
# Visualising
# ============================================================

# Plot 1: Distribution of presence percentages (top panel)
p1_summary <- ggplot(presence_summary, aes(x = Present_Percent)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7, color = "black", size = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "red3", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 96, y = max(table(cut(presence_summary$Present_Percent, 20))) * 0.9, 
           label = "317 MAGs (90.6%)", hjust = 1, color = "red3", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(90, 100, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Percentage of samples where MAG is present",
       y = "Number of indicator MAGs",
       title = "Indicator MAGs are nearly ubiquitous across all reef sites") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

# Plot 2: Simplified presence/absence heatmap (bottom panel)
# Order samples by protection status (Closed first, then Open)
metadata_for_pa$ProtectionNum <- ifelse(metadata_for_pa$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing == "C", 1, 2)
sample_order <- order(metadata_for_pa$ProtectionNum, metadata_for_pa$Sample_ID)

# Get presence/absence data ordered
presence_ordered <- presence_absence[, sample_order]

# Create a factor for MAGs based on presence frequency (least to most common)
mag_order <- presence_summary[order(presence_summary$Present_Percent), "MAG"]
presence_ordered <- presence_ordered[mag_order, ]

# Melt for ggplot
heatmap_data <- melt(as.matrix(presence_ordered))
colnames(heatmap_data) <- c("MAG", "Sample", "Presence")

# Add protection status
heatmap_data$Protection <- metadata_for_pa$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing[
  match(heatmap_data$Sample, metadata_for_pa$Sample_ID)]

# Convert to factors with proper ordering
heatmap_data$MAG <- factor(heatmap_data$MAG, levels = rev(mag_order))  # Reverse for top-to-bottom
heatmap_data$Sample <- factor(heatmap_data$Sample, levels = colnames(presence_ordered))
heatmap_data$Protection <- factor(heatmap_data$Protection, 
                                  levels = c("C", "O"),
                                  labels = c("NTMR", "Fished"))

# Create the heatmap
p2_heatmap <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = Sample, y = MAG, fill = factor(Presence))) +
  geom_tile(color = NA) +  # Remove tile borders for cleaner look
  facet_grid(~ Protection, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "white", "1" = "plum4"),
                    labels = c("Absent", "Present"),
                    name = "Presence") +
  labs(x = "Reef sites", y = "Indicator MAGs (350 total)",
       title = "Presence/absence patterns of indicator MAGs across reef sites") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),  # Hide MAG names for clarity
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.1, "lines")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "black", size = 0.5)))

# Optional: Create a version with MAG labels for the 33 least common MAGs
if(length(mags_not_all) > 0) {
  # Get the 33 MAGs not present in all samples
  subset_mags <- presence_summary$MAG[presence_summary$Present_Percent < 100]
  
  # Create a separate heatmap just for these
  subset_data <- heatmap_data[heatmap_data$MAG %in% subset_mags, ]
  
  # Create labels with taxonomy info for these MAGs
  subset_data$TaxLabel <- paste0(
    ifelse(is.na(tax_info$Genus[match(subset_data$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]) | 
           tax_info$Genus[match(subset_data$MAG, rownames(tax_info))] == "",
           tax_info$Family[match(subset_data$MAG, rownames(tax_info))],
           tax_info$Genus[match(subset_data$MAG, rownames(tax_info))]),
    "\n(", round(presence_summary$Present_Percent[match(subset_data$MAG, presence_summary$MAG)], 1), "%)"
  )
  
  # Order by presence percentage
  mag_order_subset <- presence_summary[presence_summary$MAG %in% subset_mags, ]
  mag_order_subset <- mag_order_subset[order(mag_order_subset$Present_Percent), "MAG"]
  tax_labels_ordered <- paste0(
    ifelse(is.na(tax_info$Genus[match(mag_order_subset, rownames(tax_info))]) | 
           tax_info$Genus[match(mag_order_subset, rownames(tax_info))] == "",
           tax_info$Family[match(mag_order_subset, rownames(tax_info))],
           tax_info$Genus[match(mag_order_subset, rownames(tax_info))]),
    "\n(", round(presence_summary$Present_Percent[match(mag_order_subset, presence_summary$MAG)], 1), "%)"
  )
  
  subset_data$TaxLabel <- factor(subset_data$TaxLabel, 
                                 levels = rev(tax_labels_ordered))
  
  p3_subset <- ggplot(subset_data, aes(x = Sample, y = TaxLabel, fill = factor(Presence))) +
    geom_tile(color = NA) +
    facet_grid(~ Protection, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = "white", "1" = "plum4"),
                      labels = c("Absent", "Present"),
                      name = "Presence") +
    labs(x = "Reef sites", y = "MAGs not in all sites (n=33)",
         title = "The 33 indicator MAGs with <100% presence across sites",
         subtitle = "Shown with taxonomic classification and presence percentage") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40")
    )
  
  print(p3_subset)
}

composite_plot <- p1_summary / p2_heatmap / p3_subset +
  plot_layout(heights = c(0.4, 0.4, 0.6)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Indicator MAGs are widespread across the Great Barrier Reef",
    subtitle = "350 MINT sPLS-DA selected MAGs show near-universal presence, supporting abundance-based patterns",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40")
    )
  )

ggsave("/home/marko-terzin/Documents/PhD/Thesis/Chapter_3_IMOS-MGD_MAGs/indicator_MAGs_universal_presence.pdf", 
       composite_plot, 
       width = 10, 
       height = 15,  # Increased height for the 3-panel composite
       dpi = 300)

# ***ALDEx2*** - ***A***NOVA-***L***ike ***D***ifferential ***Ex***pression tool

We will now use ALDEx2 to perform differential abundance testing per pMAG, which will complement your MINT sPLS-DA analysis and provide statistical validation of individual pMAG abundance differences between open and closed zones (while accounting for compositionality/sparsity and spatiotemporal covariates). ALDEx2 uses a Dirichlet-multinomial model to handle compositional data and provides effect sizes and false discovery rates.

## Step 1: preparing the data

```{r preparing data for ALDEx2, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# CORRECT: Use the original counts (before adding pseudocounts). From your earlier code, this is pMAGs_95ANI (before phyloseq transformation)
count_matrix <- pMAGs_95ANI  # ALDEx2 wants features (genes, taxa) as rows and samples as columns, just like mixOmics
# Open the object to verify there are zeros

# Extract metadata
ALDEx2_metadata <- as.data.frame(sample_data(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq)) %>% 
  as.matrix() %>% # Converting into a df now
  as.data.frame()

# Check alignment - reorder metadata to match count matrix
ALDEx2_metadata <- ALDEx2_metadata[colnames(count_matrix), ]
cat("Samples aligned:", identical(colnames(count_matrix), rownames(ALDEx2_metadata)), "\n")
```

## Step 2

run a simple ALDEx2 model without accounting for spatiotemporal covariates

```{r simple ALDEx2, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# APPROACH 1: Simple comparison (no covariates)
# ============================================================
cat("=== ALDEx2 Approach 1: Simple comparison (no covariates) ===\n\n")

# Ensure conditions are in correct format
conditions <- as.character(ALDEx2_metadata$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing)
cat("Condition levels:", unique(conditions), "\n")
cat("Sample sizes - Closed:", sum(conditions == "C"), "Open:", sum(conditions == "O"), "\n")

# Run ALDEx2 simple comparison
cat("\nRunning ALDEx2 simple comparison (128 Monte Carlo samples)...\n")
aldex_obj_simple <- aldex.clr(
  reads = count_matrix,
  conds = conditions,
  mc.samples = 128,
  denom = "all",  # Using "all" for denominator
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Get t-test and effect size results SEPARATELY
cat("\nCalculating t-test...\n")
aldex_ttest <- aldex.ttest(aldex_obj_simple, 
                          paired.test = FALSE,
                          hist.plot = FALSE)

cat("Calculating effect sizes...\n")
aldex_effect <- aldex.effect(aldex_obj_simple,
                            CI = TRUE,
                            include.sample.summary = FALSE)

# Combine the results
aldex_simple <- data.frame(aldex_ttest, aldex_effect)

cat("\nSimple ALDEx2 analysis completed!\n")
cat("Results dimensions:", dim(aldex_simple), "\n")
cat("\nFirst few results:\n")
print(head(aldex_simple))
```

### Visualisation

```{r simple ALDEx2 results, fig.height=8, fig.width=14, fig.cap="ALDEx2 analysis (simple model) comparing pMAG abundances between No-Take Marine Reserves (NTMRs) and fished reefs (n = 876 MAGs). (a) Volcano plot showing effect sizes (log₂ fold change) against FDR-adjusted p-values. Red points indicate significant pMAGs (FDR < 0.05), with positive effects enriched in fished reefs and negative effects in NTMRs. (b) Distribution of raw p-values (Welch's t-test). (c) Distribution of effect sizes (mean = X). (d) Distribution of overlap statistics, measuring effect certainty. ", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# QUICK RESULTS CHECK
# ============================================================

cat("=== QUICK RESULTS CHECK ===\n\n")

# 1. Basic statistics
cat("1. Basic Statistics:\n")
cat("   Total MAGs tested:", nrow(aldex_simple), "\n")
cat("   Mean p-value (Welch's):", mean(aldex_simple$we.ep, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("   Mean p-value (Wilcoxon):", mean(aldex_simple$wi.ep, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("   Mean effect size:", mean(aldex_simple$effect, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("   Effect size range:", range(aldex_simple$effect, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# 2. Significance with different thresholds
cat("\n2. Significance at different thresholds:\n")

# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction
aldex_simple$we.eBH <- p.adjust(aldex_simple$we.ep, method = "BH")
aldex_simple$wi.eBH <- p.adjust(aldex_simple$wi.ep, method = "BH")

for(alpha in c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001)) {
  sig_we <- sum(aldex_simple$we.eBH < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  sig_wi <- sum(aldex_simple$wi.eBH < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("   FDR < %.3f: Welch = %d, Wilcoxon = %d\n", alpha, sig_we, sig_wi))
}

# 3. Effect size distribution
cat("\n3. Effect Size Distribution:\n")
effect_categories <- cut(abs(aldex_simple$effect),
                         breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, Inf),
                         labels = c("Very small (<0.5)", "Small (0.5-1)", 
                                   "Medium (1-2)", "Large (>2)"))
cat("   Effect size categories:\n")
print(table(effect_categories))

# 4. Direction of effects
cat("\n4. Direction of Effects (using FDR < 0.05, Welch's test):\n")
sig_idx <- aldex_simple$we.eBH < 0.05
if(any(sig_idx)) {
  sig_effects <- aldex_simple$effect[sig_idx]
  cat("   Enriched in Open zones (positive effect):", sum(sig_effects > 0), "\n")
  cat("   Enriched in Closed zones (negative effect):", sum(sig_effects < 0), "\n")
  cat("   Mean effect in significant MAGs:", mean(sig_effects), "\n")
} else {
  cat("   No significant MAGs at FDR < 0.05\n")
}

# ============================================================
# QUICK VISUALIZATIONS
# ============================================================

# Set significance threshold
aldex_simple$significant <- aldex_simple$we.eBH < 0.05

# 1. Volcano plot (main result)
p1 <- ggplot(aldex_simple, aes(x = effect, y = -log10(we.eBH))) +
  geom_point(aes(color = significant, size = significant), alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray70", "TRUE" = "red3")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(1, 2)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 0, 1), linetype = c("dashed", "solid", "dashed"), 
             color = c("blue", "black", "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Effect size (log2 fold change)", 
       y = "-log₁₀(FDR-adjusted p-value)",
       title = "ALDEx2: Open vs. Closed Reef Zones",
       subtitle = paste(sum(aldex_simple$significant), "significant MAGs (FDR < 0.05)")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# 2. P-value distribution
p2 <- ggplot(aldex_simple, aes(x = -log10(we.ep))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "-log₁₀(raw p-value)", y = "Frequency",
       title = "P-value Distribution",
       subtitle = paste("Expected uniform under null")) +
  theme_minimal()

# 3. Effect size distribution
p3 <- ggplot(aldex_simple, aes(x = effect)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "seagreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Effect size", y = "Frequency",
       title = "Effect Size Distribution",
       subtitle = paste("Mean =", round(mean(aldex_simple$effect), 3))) +
  theme_minimal()

# 4. Overlap plot (shows reproducibility)
p4 <- ggplot(aldex_simple, aes(x = overlap)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Overlap", y = "Frequency",
       title = "Overlap Distribution",
       subtitle = "Measure of effect certainty") +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine plots
(p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) + 
  plot_annotation(title = "ALDEx2 Quick Diagnostics",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)))
```

Checking for the test agreement:

```{r simple ALDEx2 test consistency, fig.cap="Consistency between statistical tests for differential abundance detection. Scatter plot comparing -log₁₀ transformed p-values from Welch's t-test (x-axis) and Wilcoxon rank-sum test (y-axis) for detecting differentially abundant MAGs between reef protection zones. The red dashed line indicates perfect agreement (y = x). 283 of 305 significant MAGs (FDR < 0.05) were identified by both tests, supporting robust identification of protection-associated taxa.", fig.height=3, fig.width=5, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# CHECK TEST CONSISTENCY
# ============================================================

cat("\n=== TEST CONSISTENCY CHECK ===\n\n")

# Compare Welch vs Wilcoxon results
aldex_simple$sig_welch <- aldex_simple$we.eBH < 0.05
aldex_simple$sig_wilcox <- aldex_simple$wi.eBH < 0.05

cat("Agreement between Welch and Wilcoxon tests:\n")
cat("   Both significant:", sum(aldex_simple$sig_welch & aldex_simple$sig_wilcox), "\n")
cat("   Welch only:", sum(aldex_simple$sig_welch & !aldex_simple$sig_wilcox), "\n")
cat("   Wilcoxon only:", sum(!aldex_simple$sig_welch & aldex_simple$sig_wilcox), "\n")
cat("   Neither:", sum(!aldex_simple$sig_welch & !aldex_simple$sig_wilcox), "\n")

# Correlation between p-values
cor_test <- cor.test(-log10(aldex_simple$we.ep), -log10(aldex_simple$wi.ep), 
                     method = "spearman")
cat("\nCorrelation between test statistics:\n")
cat("   Spearman's rho:", round(cor_test$estimate, 3), "\n")
cat("   p-value:", format(cor_test$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n")

# Quick plot of test agreement
p_test_agree <- ggplot(aldex_simple, aes(x = -log10(we.ep), y = -log10(wi.ep))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "-log₁₀(Welch p-value)", y = "-log₁₀(Wilcoxon p-value)",
       title = "Test Agreement",
       subtitle = paste("Spearman's ρ =", round(cor_test$estimate, 3))) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_test_agree)
```

Visualising the indicators at genus level:

```{r simple ALDEx2 genus level indicators, fig.height=8, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Genus-level patterns of differentially abundant MAGs between reef protection zones. (a) Bar chart showing the number of significant MAGs belonging to the 15 most abundant genera, separated by enrichment in fished (blue) versus No-Take Marine Reserve (NTMR; green) zones. (b) Pie chart showing the overall distribution of significant MAGs between zones. (c) Bubble plot displaying genus-level enrichment patterns, where point size represents total significant MAGs per genus, position on the x-axis shows net enrichment (positive = NTMR-enriched, negative = fished-enriched), and color indicates the dominant zone of enrichment.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# GENUS-LEVEL ANALYSIS OF SIGNIFICANT MAGS
# ============================================================
cat("=== GENUS-LEVEL ANALYSIS ===\n\n")

# Add taxonomy to significant MAGs
aldex_simple$significant <- aldex_simple$we.eBH < 0.05
aldex_simple_tax <- cbind(
  aldex_simple,
  tax_table(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq)[rownames(aldex_simple), ]
)

# Get significant MAGs
sig_mags <- aldex_simple_tax[aldex_simple_tax$significant, ]

cat("Total significant MAGs:", nrow(sig_mags), "\n")
cat("MAGs with genus assignment:", sum(!is.na(sig_mags$Genus) & sig_mags$Genus != ""), "\n\n")

# Separate by enrichment direction
sig_mags$enrichment <- ifelse(sig_mags$effect > 0, 
                             "Enriched_in_Open", 
                             "Enriched_in_Closed")

# 1. Count unique genera in each group
cat("1. Unique genera by enrichment direction:\n")
genera_open <- unique(sig_mags$Genus[sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Open"])
genera_closed <- unique(sig_mags$Genus[sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Closed"])

cat("   Genera enriched in Open zones:", length(genera_open[!is.na(genera_open) & genera_open != ""]), "\n")
cat("   Genera enriched in Closed zones:", length(genera_closed[!is.na(genera_closed) & genera_closed != ""]), "\n")
cat("   Overlap (genera in both groups):", length(intersect(genera_open, genera_closed)), "\n\n")

# 2. Most frequent genera in each group
cat("2. Top 10 most frequent genera in each group:\n\n")

# Open zones (positive effect)
open_genera_counts <- sort(table(sig_mags$Genus[sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Open"]), 
                          decreasing = TRUE)
open_genera_counts <- open_genera_counts[names(open_genera_counts) != "" & 
                                         !is.na(names(open_genera_counts))]

cat("   Enriched in OPEN zones (fished reefs):\n")
if(length(open_genera_counts) > 0) {
  top_open <- head(open_genera_counts, 10)
  for(i in 1:length(top_open)) {
    cat(sprintf("      %-30s: %3d MAGs\n", names(top_open)[i], top_open[i]))
  }
} else {
  cat("      No genus assignments\n")
}

# Closed zones (negative effect)  
closed_genera_counts <- sort(table(sig_mags$Genus[sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Closed"]), 
                            decreasing = TRUE)
closed_genera_counts <- closed_genera_counts[names(closed_genera_counts) != "" & 
                                            !is.na(names(closed_genera_counts))]

cat("\n   Enriched in CLOSED zones (MPAs/no-take):\n")
if(length(closed_genera_counts) > 0) {
  top_closed <- head(closed_genera_counts, 10)
  for(i in 1:length(top_closed)) {
    cat(sprintf("      %-30s: %3d MAGs\n", names(top_closed)[i], top_closed[i]))
  }
} else {
  cat("      No genus assignments\n")
}

# 3. Create a summary data frame
cat("\n3. Creating summary table...\n")

# Get all unique genera with assignments
all_genera <- unique(sig_mags$Genus)
all_genera <- all_genera[!is.na(all_genera) & all_genera != ""]

if(length(all_genera) > 0) {
  genus_summary <- data.frame(
    Genus = all_genera,
    MAGs_Open = sapply(all_genera, function(g) sum(sig_mags$Genus == g & sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Open", na.rm = TRUE)),
    MAGs_Closed = sapply(all_genera, function(g) sum(sig_mags$Genus == g & sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Closed", na.rm = TRUE)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Calculate totals and net enrichment
  genus_summary$Total_MAGs <- genus_summary$MAGs_Open + genus_summary$MAGs_Closed
  genus_summary$Net_Enrichment <- genus_summary$MAGs_Closed - genus_summary$MAGs_Open
  genus_summary$Dominant_Zone <- ifelse(genus_summary$Net_Enrichment > 0, "Closed", 
                                       ifelse(genus_summary$Net_Enrichment < 0, "Open", "Mixed"))
  
  # Sort by total MAGs
  genus_summary <- genus_summary[order(-genus_summary$Total_MAGs), ]
  
  cat("\nTop 20 genera with most significant MAGs:\n")
  print(head(genus_summary, 20))
  
  # Save to file
  write.csv(genus_summary, 
            "ALDEx2_genus_summary.csv",
            row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nGenus summary saved to: ALDEx2_genus_summary.csv\n")
} else {
  cat("No genus assignments found in significant MAGs\n")
}

# ============================================================
# VISUALIZE GENUS-LEVEL PATTERNS
# ============================================================
if(exists("genus_summary") && nrow(genus_summary) > 0) {
  
  # 1. Bar plot: Top genera by total significant MAGs
  top_genera <- head(genus_summary[order(-genus_summary$Total_MAGs), ], 15)
  top_genera_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
    top_genera,
    cols = c("MAGs_Open", "MAGs_Closed"),
    names_to = "Zone",
    values_to = "Count"
  )
  top_genera_long$Zone <- gsub("MAGs_", "", top_genera_long$Zone)
  
  p1 <- ggplot(top_genera_long, aes(x = reorder(Genus, -Count), y = Count, fill = Zone)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Open" = "steelblue4", "Closed" = "seagreen3"),
                      labels = c("Open" = "Fished", "Closed" = "MPA")) +
    labs(x = "Genus", y = "Number of Significant MAGs",
         title = "Top Genera with Most Significant MAGs",
         subtitle = "Comparing fished vs. marine protected areas") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # 2. Bubble plot: MAG count vs net enrichment
  p2 <- ggplot(genus_summary, aes(x = Net_Enrichment, y = Total_MAGs)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Total_MAGs, color = Dominant_Zone), alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Closed" = "seagreen3", "Open" = "steelblue4", "Mixed" = "gray70"),
                       labels = c("Closed" = "MPA-enriched", "Open" = "Fished-enriched", "Mixed" = "Mixed")) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    labs(x = "Net Enrichment (Closed - Open)",
         y = "Total Significant MAGs",
         title = "Genus-Level Enrichment Patterns",
         subtitle = paste("Positive values = MPA-enriched, Negative = Fished-enriched\n",
                         nrow(genus_summary), "genera with significant MAGs")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # 3. Stacked bar: Overall distribution
  overall_counts <- data.frame(
    Zone = c("Open (Fished)", "Closed (MPA)"),
    Count = c(sum(sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Open"),
              sum(sig_mags$enrichment == "Enriched_in_Closed"))
  )
  
  p3 <- ggplot(overall_counts, aes(x = "", y = Count, fill = Zone)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
    coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Open (Fished)" = "steelblue4", "Closed (MPA)" = "seagreen3")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         title = "Overall Distribution of Significant MAGs",
         subtitle = paste("Total:", sum(overall_counts$Count), "MAGs")) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  
  # Combine plots
  library(patchwork)
  (p1 + p3) / p2 + 
    plot_annotation(title = "Genus-Level Analysis of Reef Protection Effects",
                    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16)))
  
} else {
  cat("No genus data available for visualization\n")
}
