## ***Complex ALDEx2*** GLM model with spatiotemporal covariates

Now let's implement the complex ALDEx2 GLM model with spatiotemporal covariates, and compare it with both the simple model and MINT sPLS-DA:

```{r complex ALDEx2 GLM model with spatiotemporal covariates, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# COMPLEX MODEL: ALDEx2 GLM with spatiotemporal covariates
# ============================================================
cat("=== ALDEx2 Approach 2: GLM with covariates (sampling trip + sector) ===\n\n")

# Create the MODEL MATRIX for the GLM
cat("Creating model matrix for GLM...\n")
model_matrix <- model.matrix(~ Open_or_Closed_to_fishing + 
                               Sampling_trip + 
                               SECTOR_N_S, 
                             data = ALDEx2_metadata)

cat("Model matrix dimensions:", dim(model_matrix), "\n")
cat("Model matrix columns:\n")
print(colnames(model_matrix))

# Identify the protection status coefficient
protection_col <- grep("Open_or_Closed", colnames(model_matrix), value = TRUE)[1]
cat("\nProtection status coefficient:", protection_col, "\n")

# Run ALDEx2 with the model matrix DIRECTLY
cat("\nRunning ALDEx2 GLM with model matrix (128 Monte Carlo samples)...\n")

aldex_obj_glm <- aldex.clr(
  reads = count_matrix,
  conds = model_matrix,  # Use the model matrix directly here!
  mc.samples = 128,
  denom = "all",
  verbose = TRUE
)

# Now extract the GLM results
cat("\nExtracting GLM results...\n")
aldex_glm_results <- aldex.glm(aldex_obj_glm)

# The results will contain coefficients for each term in your model
cat("\nGLM results structure:\n")
print(str(aldex_glm_results, max.level = 1))

# Extract results for ALL terms in the model
extract_term_results <- function(aldex_glm_results, term_name) {
  est_col <- paste0(term_name, ":Est")
  se_col <- paste0(term_name, ":SE")
  t_col <- paste0(term_name, ":t.val")
  p_col <- paste0(term_name, ":pval")
  padj_col <- paste0(term_name, ":pval.padj")
  
  if (all(c(est_col, se_col, t_col, p_col, padj_col) %in% colnames(aldex_glm_results))) {
    results <- data.frame(
      Taxon = rownames(aldex_glm_results),
      Effect_Estimate = aldex_glm_results[, est_col],
      Std_Error = aldex_glm_results[, se_col],
      t_value = aldex_glm_results[, t_col],
      p_value = aldex_glm_results[, p_col],
      p_adj = aldex_glm_results[, padj_col]
    )
    return(results)
  }
  return(NULL)
}

# Extract for each term
model_terms <- colnames(model_matrix)[-1]  # Exclude intercept
for (term in model_terms) {
  cat("\n=== Results for:", term, "===\n")
  term_results <- extract_term_results(aldex_glm_results, term)
  if (!is.null(term_results)) {
    # Sort by p-value
    term_results <- term_results[order(term_results$p_value), ]
    sig_count <- sum(term_results$p_adj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
    cat("Significant taxa at FDR < 0.05:", sig_count, "\n")
    if (sig_count > 0) {
      print(head(term_results[term_results$p_adj < 0.05, ], 10))
    }
  }
}

# ============================================================
# COMPLETE THE GLM ANALYSIS WITH TAXONOMY
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== ADDING TAXONOMY TO GLM RESULTS ===\n\n")

# First, extract the protection status results from the GLM
protection_term <- "Open_or_Closed_to_fishingO"
glm_protection_results <- extract_term_results(aldex_glm_results, protection_term)

if (!is.null(glm_protection_results)) {
  # Get taxonomy table
  tax_table_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq))
  
  # Check rowname matches
  cat("Checking taxonomy matches...\n")
  matching_taxa <- glm_protection_results$Taxon[glm_protection_results$Taxon %in% rownames(tax_table_df)]
  cat("Taxa with taxonomy info:", length(matching_taxa), "/", nrow(glm_protection_results), "\n")
  
  # Add taxonomy to GLM results
  # Sort both dataframes by Taxon to ensure alignment
  glm_protection_results <- glm_protection_results[order(glm_protection_results$Taxon), ]
  tax_table_df <- tax_table_df[order(rownames(tax_table_df)), ]
  
  # Combine taxonomy with GLM results
  aldex_glm_tax <- cbind(
    glm_protection_results,
    tax_table_df[glm_protection_results$Taxon, ]
  )
  
  cat("\nGLM results with taxonomy - structure:\n")
  print(str(aldex_glm_tax, max.level = 1))
  
  # Apply FDR correction (though ALDEx2 already provides it)
  # Let's use the p_adj column that ALDEx2 already calculated
  if ("p_adj" %in% colnames(aldex_glm_tax)) {
    aldex_glm_tax$GLM_FDR <- aldex_glm_tax$p_adj
  } else {
    aldex_glm_tax$GLM_FDR <- p.adjust(aldex_glm_tax$p_value, method = "BH")
  }
  
  aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant <- aldex_glm_tax$GLM_FDR < 0.05
  
  # Calculate GLM effect direction
  # Positive effect = enriched in Open zones
  # Negative effect = enriched in Closed zones
  aldex_glm_tax$GLM_enrichment <- ifelse(aldex_glm_tax$Effect_Estimate > 0,
                                        "Enriched_in_Open_GLM",
                                        "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM")
  
  cat("\nGLM SIGNIFICANCE SUMMARY (with covariates):\n")
  cat("===========================================\n")
  cat("Total MAGs analyzed:", nrow(aldex_glm_tax), "\n")
  cat("Significant MAGs in GLM (FDR < 0.05):", sum(aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("Enriched in Open zones (positive effect):", 
      sum(aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant & aldex_glm_tax$Effect_Estimate > 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("Enriched in Closed zones (negative effect):", 
      sum(aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant & aldex_glm_tax$Effect_Estimate < 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  
  # Show top significant results
  cat("\nTOP 10 SIGNIFICANT MAGS IN GLM MODEL:\n")
  sig_mags_glm <- aldex_glm_tax[aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant, ]
  sig_mags_glm <- sig_mags_glm[order(sig_mags_glm$p_value), ]
  print(head(sig_mags_glm[, c("Taxon", "Effect_Estimate", "p_value", "GLM_FDR", "GLM_enrichment")], 10))
  
  # Save the full GLM results
  write.csv(aldex_glm_tax, "aldex2_glm_full_results_with_taxonomy.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nFull GLM results saved to: aldex2_glm_full_results_with_taxonomy.csv\n")
  
} else {
  cat("\nERROR: Could not extract protection status results from GLM.\n")
}
```

```{r simple vs complex ALDEx2 comparison, fig.height=8, fig.width=12, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# COMPARE SIMPLE vs. GLM MODELS (FIXED)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== COMPARING SIMPLE vs. GLM MODELS ===\n\n")

# First, ensure we have both results with taxonomy
# For simple model (from your earlier code)
aldex_simple_tax <- cbind(
  aldex_simple,
  tax_table(pMAGs_95ANI_phyloseq)[rownames(aldex_simple), ]
)

# Add Taxon column to simple results (using rownames)
aldex_simple_tax$Taxon <- rownames(aldex_simple_tax)

# Add significance and enrichment for simple model
aldex_simple_tax$simple_significant <- aldex_simple_tax$we.eBH < 0.05
aldex_simple_tax$simple_enrichment <- ifelse(aldex_simple_tax$effect > 0,
                                            "Enriched_in_Open_simple",
                                            "Enriched_in_Closed_simple")

# Now compare if we have both results
if (exists("aldex_glm_tax") && exists("aldex_simple_tax")) {
  # Create comparison dataframe
  simple_for_merge <- aldex_simple_tax[, c("Taxon", "effect", "we.eBH", "simple_significant", "simple_enrichment")]
  glm_for_merge <- aldex_glm_tax[, c("Taxon", "Effect_Estimate", "GLM_FDR", "GLM_significant", "GLM_enrichment")]
  
  # Merge on Taxon
  comparison_df <- merge(simple_for_merge, glm_for_merge, by = "Taxon", all = TRUE)
  
  cat("COMPARISON SUMMARY:\n")
  cat("===================\n")
  cat("Total MAGs in comparison:", nrow(comparison_df), "\n\n")
  
  # Agreement between models
  cat("AGREEMENT BETWEEN MODELS (FDR < 0.05):\n")
  cat("Both significant:", 
      sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("Simple model only:", 
      sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & !comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("GLM model only:", 
      sum(!comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("Neither significant:", 
      sum(!comparison_df$simple_significant & !comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE), "\n\n")
  
  # Check effect direction consistency among significant MAGs in both models
  both_sig <- comparison_df[comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, ]
  if (nrow(both_sig) > 0) {
    cat("CONSISTENCY IN EFFECT DIRECTION (when both significant):\n")
    # Extract enrichment direction (Open vs Closed)
    both_sig$simple_direction <- ifelse(both_sig$effect > 0, "Open", "Closed")
    both_sig$glm_direction <- ifelse(both_sig$Effect_Estimate > 0, "Open", "Closed")
    
    agreement <- sum(both_sig$simple_direction == both_sig$glm_direction)
    cat("Agreement in enrichment direction:", agreement, "/", nrow(both_sig), 
        sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", agreement/nrow(both_sig)*100))
  }
  
  # Correlation between effect sizes
  cat("\nCORRELATION BETWEEN EFFECT SIZES:\n")
  cor_simple_glm <- cor.test(comparison_df$effect, comparison_df$Effect_Estimate, 
                            method = "spearman", na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Spearman correlation:", round(cor_simple_glm$estimate, 3), "\n")
  cat("p-value:", format(cor_simple_glm$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3), "\n")
  
  # Save comparison
  write.csv(comparison_df, "aldex2_simple_vs_glm_comparison.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nComparison saved to: aldex2_simple_vs_glm_comparison.csv\n")
  
} else {
  cat("Cannot compare models: one or both results not available.\n")
}
```

```{r complex ALDEx2 genus level analysis, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# GENUS-LEVEL ANALYSIS FOR GLM RESULTS
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== GENUS-LEVEL ANALYSIS FOR GLM MODEL ===\n\n")

if (exists("aldex_glm_tax")) {
  # Get significant MAGs from GLM
  sig_mags_glm <- aldex_glm_tax[aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant, ]
  
  cat("Total significant MAGs in GLM:", nrow(sig_mags_glm), "\n")
  cat("MAGs with genus assignment:", 
      sum(!is.na(sig_mags_glm$Genus) & sig_mags_glm$Genus != ""), "\n\n")
  
  # Separate by enrichment direction
  sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction <- ifelse(sig_mags_glm$Effect_Estimate > 0, 
                                             "Enriched_in_Open_GLM", 
                                             "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM")
  
  # 1. Count unique genera in each group
  cat("1. UNIQUE GENERA BY ENRICHMENT DIRECTION (GLM):\n")
  genera_open_glm <- unique(sig_mags_glm$Genus[sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Open_GLM"])
  genera_closed_glm <- unique(sig_mags_glm$Genus[sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM"])
  
  cat("   Genera enriched in Open zones (fished):", 
      length(genera_open_glm[!is.na(genera_open_glm) & genera_open_glm != ""]), "\n")
  cat("   Genera enriched in Closed zones (MPA):", 
      length(genera_closed_glm[!is.na(genera_closed_glm) & genera_closed_glm != ""]), "\n")
  cat("   Overlap (genera in both groups):", 
      length(intersect(genera_open_glm, genera_closed_glm)), "\n\n")
  
  # 2. Most frequent genera in each group (GLM)
  cat("2. TOP 10 MOST FREQUENT GENERA IN EACH GROUP (GLM):\n\n")
  
  # Open zones (positive effect) - GLM
  open_genera_counts_glm <- sort(table(sig_mags_glm$Genus[sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Open_GLM"]), 
                               decreasing = TRUE)
  open_genera_counts_glm <- open_genera_counts_glm[names(open_genera_counts_glm) != "" & 
                                                  !is.na(names(open_genera_counts_glm))]
  
  cat("   Enriched in OPEN zones (fished reefs) - GLM:\n")
  if(length(open_genera_counts_glm) > 0) {
    top_open_glm <- head(open_genera_counts_glm, 10)
    for(i in 1:length(top_open_glm)) {
      cat(sprintf("      %-30s: %3d MAGs\n", names(top_open_glm)[i], top_open_glm[i]))
    }
  } else {
    cat("      No genus assignments\n")
  }
  
  # Closed zones (negative effect) - GLM
  closed_genera_counts_glm <- sort(table(sig_mags_glm$Genus[sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM"]), 
                                 decreasing = TRUE)
  closed_genera_counts_glm <- closed_genera_counts_glm[names(closed_genera_counts_glm) != "" & 
                                                      !is.na(names(closed_genera_counts_glm))]
  
  cat("\n   Enriched in CLOSED zones (MPAs) - GLM:\n")
  if(length(closed_genera_counts_glm) > 0) {
    top_closed_glm <- head(closed_genera_counts_glm, 10)
    for(i in 1:length(top_closed_glm)) {
      cat(sprintf("      %-30s: %3d MAGs\n", names(top_closed_glm)[i], top_closed_glm[i]))
    }
  } else {
    cat("      No genus assignments\n")
  }
  
  # 3. Create genus summary for GLM
  cat("\n3. CREATING GENUS SUMMARY TABLE FOR GLM...\n")
  
  # Get all unique genera with assignments from GLM results
  all_genera_glm <- unique(sig_mags_glm$Genus)
  all_genera_glm <- all_genera_glm[!is.na(all_genera_glm) & all_genera_glm != ""]
  
  if(length(all_genera_glm) > 0) {
    genus_summary_glm <- data.frame(
      Genus = all_genera_glm,
      MAGs_Open_GLM = sapply(all_genera_glm, function(g) 
        sum(sig_mags_glm$Genus == g & sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Open_GLM", na.rm = TRUE)),
      MAGs_Closed_GLM = sapply(all_genera_glm, function(g) 
        sum(sig_mags_glm$Genus == g & sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM", na.rm = TRUE)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    # Calculate totals and net enrichment
    genus_summary_glm$Total_MAGs_GLM <- genus_summary_glm$MAGs_Open_GLM + genus_summary_glm$MAGs_Closed_GLM
    genus_summary_glm$Net_Enrichment_GLM <- genus_summary_glm$MAGs_Closed_GLM - genus_summary_glm$MAGs_Open_GLM
    genus_summary_glm$Dominant_Zone_GLM <- ifelse(genus_summary_glm$Net_Enrichment_GLM > 0, "Closed_GLM", 
                                                 ifelse(genus_summary_glm$Net_Enrichment_GLM < 0, "Open_GLM", "Mixed_GLM"))
    
    # Sort by total MAGs
    genus_summary_glm <- genus_summary_glm[order(-genus_summary_glm$Total_MAGs_GLM), ]
    
    cat("\nTop 20 genera with most significant MAGs in GLM model:\n")
    print(head(genus_summary_glm, 20))
    
    # Save to file
    write.csv(genus_summary_glm, 
              "ALDEx2_GLM_genus_summary.csv",
              row.names = FALSE)
    cat("\nGLM genus summary saved to: ALDEx2_GLM_genus_summary.csv\n")
  } else {
    cat("No genus assignments found in significant MAGs from GLM model\n")
  }
  
} else {
  cat("GLM taxonomy results not available for genus-level analysis.\n")
}
```

```{r simple vs complex ALDEx2 VISUALIZE THE COMPARISON, fig.height=8, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Statistical validation of indicator MAGs using per-MAG differential abundance testing. (A) Agreement between significance calls in simple (no covariates) versus GLM models (with spatiotemporal covariates). Of 876 MAGs tested, 237 were significant in both models, representing robust reef protection signals. (B) Correlation of effect sizes between models shows strong agreement (Spearman ρ = r round(cor_simple_glm$estimate, 3), p < 0.001), with 100% consistency in enrichment direction for overlapping significant MAGs. Colors indicate MAGs significant in both models (red), simple model only (blue; potential false positives), GLM model only (green; signals unmasked by covariate adjustment), or neither (gray). (C) Distribution of FDR-adjusted p-values demonstrates similar statistical power between models, with both showing enrichment of significant signals beyond the null expectation (dashed red line at -log₁₀(0.05)). Together, these analyses validate the robustness of MINT sPLS-DA indicator selection while highlighting the importance of accounting for spatiotemporal confounding.",eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# VISUALIZE THE COMPARISON
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== VISUALIZING SIMPLE vs. GLM COMPARISON ===\n\n")

if (exists("comparison_df")) {
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  
  # 1. Venn diagram-style comparison (using a bar plot)
  comparison_summary <- data.frame(
    Category = c("Both significant", "Simple only", "GLM only", "Neither"),
    Count = c(
      sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & !comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(!comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(!comparison_df$simple_significant & !comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
  
  p1 <- ggplot(comparison_summary, aes(x = reorder(Category, -Count), y = Count, fill = Category)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.5) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(x = "Significance Category", y = "Number of MAGs",
         title = "Comparison of Significance Calls",
         subtitle = "Simple vs. GLM model (FDR < 0.05)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.position = "none")
  
  # 2. Scatter plot of effect sizes
  p2 <- ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = effect, y = Effect_Estimate)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = ifelse(simple_significant & GLM_significant, "Both",
                                  ifelse(simple_significant, "Simple only",
                                         ifelse(GLM_significant, "GLM only", "Neither")))), 
               alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Both" = "red3", 
                                  "Simple only" = "steelblue4", 
                                  "GLM only" = "seagreen3",
                                  "Neither" = "gray70"),
                       name = "Significance") +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +
    labs(x = "Effect size (Simple model)", 
         y = "Effect size (GLM model)",
         title = "Effect Size Comparison",
         subtitle = paste("Spearman ρ =", round(cor_simple_glm$estimate, 3))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # 3. Distribution of p-values in both models
  p3_data <- data.frame(
    Model = rep(c("Simple", "GLM"), each = nrow(comparison_df)),
    p_value = c(-log10(comparison_df$we.eBH), -log10(comparison_df$GLM_FDR))
  )
  
  p3 <- ggplot(p3_data, aes(x = p_value, fill = Model)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    labs(x = "-log₁₀(FDR-adjusted p-value)", y = "Density",
         title = "Distribution of P-values",
         subtitle = "Comparison between models") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # Combine plots
  print(p1 + p2 + p3 + plot_layout(ncol = 2))
  
  cat("\nVisualizations created.\n")
  
  # 4. Create a summary table of key differences
  cat("\nKEY FINDINGS SUMMARY:\n")
  cat("=====================\n")
  
  # MAGs that lost significance in GLM (likely spurious due to covariates)
  lost_sig <- comparison_df[comparison_df$simple_significant & !comparison_df$GLM_significant, ]
  cat("\n1. MAGs that lost significance in GLM (likely false positives in simple model):", 
      nrow(lost_sig), "\n")
  
  # MAGs that gained significance in GLM (likely true signals masked by covariates)
  gained_sig <- comparison_df[!comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, ]
  cat("2. MAGs that gained significance in GLM (unmasked by covariate adjustment):", 
      nrow(gained_sig), "\n")
  
  # Check if effect sizes changed direction
  both_sig <- comparison_df[comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, ]
  if (nrow(both_sig) > 0) {
    direction_changes <- sum((both_sig$effect > 0) != (both_sig$Effect_Estimate > 0))
    cat("3. MAGs significant in both but changed direction:", direction_changes, "/", nrow(both_sig),
        sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", direction_changes/nrow(both_sig)*100))
  }
  
} else {
  cat("Comparison dataframe not available for visualization.\n")
}
```

```{r create-aldex-comparison-objects, include=FALSE}
# Create both_sig_df for direction consistency check
both_sig_df <- comparison_df[comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, ]
if(nrow(both_sig_df) > 0) {
  both_sig_df$simple_direction <- ifelse(both_sig_df$effect > 0, "Open", "Closed")
  both_sig_df$glm_direction <- ifelse(both_sig_df$Effect_Estimate > 0, "Open", "Closed")
} else {
  both_sig_df <- data.frame(
    simple_direction = character(0),
    glm_direction = character(0)
  )
}

# Get GLM genus data
sig_mags_glm <- aldex_glm_tax[aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant, ]
sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction <- ifelse(sig_mags_glm$Effect_Estimate > 0, 
                                           "Enriched_in_Open_GLM", 
                                           "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM")

genera_open_glm <- unique(sig_mags_glm$Genus[sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Open_GLM"])
genera_closed_glm <- unique(sig_mags_glm$Genus[sig_mags_glm$enrichment_direction == "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM"])

# Calculate correlation if not already done
if(!exists("cor_simple_glm")) {
  cor_simple_glm <- cor.test(comparison_df$effect, comparison_df$Effect_Estimate, 
                            method = "spearman", na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

**Key Finding:** When accounting for spatiotemporal covariates (sampling trip + sector), the GLM model confirms the majority of indicator MAGs identified by the simple model, with strong agreement in effect sizes and enrichment directions.

### Model Agreement Statistics

**Significance Overlap:**
- **Total MAGs analyzed:** `r nrow(comparison_df)`
- **Simple model significant (FDR < 0.05):** `r sum(comparison_df$simple_significant, na.rm = TRUE)`
- **GLM model with covariates significant (FDR < 0.05):** `r sum(comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)`
- **Robust indicators (both models significant):** `r sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)` (`r round(sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)/sum(comparison_df$simple_significant, na.rm = TRUE)*100, 1)`% of simple model MAGs)
- **Potential false positives (simple model only):** `r sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & !comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)`
- **Unmasked signals (GLM model only):** `r sum(!comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)`

**Enrichment Patterns:**
- **Simple model - Enriched in Open zones:** `r sum(aldex_simple_tax$simple_significant & aldex_simple_tax$simple_enrichment == "Enriched_in_Open_simple", na.rm = TRUE)` MAGs
- **Simple model - Enriched in Closed zones:** `r sum(aldex_simple_tax$simple_significant & aldex_simple_tax$simple_enrichment == "Enriched_in_Closed_simple", na.rm = TRUE)` MAGs
- **GLM model - Enriched in Open zones:** `r sum(aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant & aldex_glm_tax$GLM_enrichment == "Enriched_in_Open_GLM", na.rm = TRUE)` MAGs
- **GLM model - Enriched in Closed zones:** `r sum(aldex_glm_tax$GLM_significant & aldex_glm_tax$GLM_enrichment == "Enriched_in_Closed_GLM", na.rm = TRUE)` MAGs

**Agreement Metrics:**
- **Effect size correlation (Spearman ρ):** `r round(cor_simple_glm$estimate, 3)` (p = `r format(cor_simple_glm$p.value, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`)
- **Direction consistency (both models significant):** `r sum(both_sig_df$simple_direction == both_sig_df$glm_direction)`/`r nrow(both_sig_df)` MAGs (`r round(sum(both_sig_df$simple_direction == both_sig_df$glm_direction)/nrow(both_sig_df)*100, 1)`% agreement)

**Genus-Level Summary (GLM Model):**
- **Total significant MAGs in GLM:** `r nrow(sig_mags_glm)`
- **Unique genera enriched in Open zones:** `r length(genera_open_glm[!is.na(genera_open_glm) & genera_open_glm != ""])`
- **Unique genera enriched in Closed zones:** `r length(genera_closed_glm[!is.na(genera_closed_glm) & genera_closed_glm != ""])`
- **Genera showing mixed enrichment patterns:** `r length(intersect(genera_open_glm, genera_closed_glm))`

**Interpretation:** The high overlap between models (`r round(sum(comparison_df$simple_significant & comparison_df$GLM_significant, na.rm = TRUE)/sum(comparison_df$simple_significant, na.rm = TRUE)*100, 1)`% of simple model MAGs confirmed by GLM) suggests robust protection-associated microbial signatures. The GLM model refines the simple model by controlling for spatiotemporal variation while largely preserving the core indicator taxa.

# MINT sPLS-DA with ***Read-based metagenomics*** data - do the same indicator taxa respond to zoning?

Independent Verification with Read-Based Analysis: To further reinforce the patterns, we will add results from an independent analysis that does not rely on MAGs at all. We have previously performed differential abundance testing on metagenomic reads classified directly against the NCBI nr database (see Terzin et al. 2025; Microbiome). This approach is free from any biases introduced by MAG binning, completeness, or genome size estimation. The consistent identification of similar taxonomic indicators through this orthogonal method strongly argues that the observed patterns are biological and not methodological artifacts.

### Tuning the number of dimensions

The perf() function is used to estimate the performance of the MINT-sPLS-DA model using ***L***eave ***O***ne ***G***roup ***O***ut ***C***ross Validation (LOGOCV), and to choose the optimal number of components for our final model

```{r read-based Open and closed to fishing sector, fig.height=6, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Choosing the number of components in mint.splsda using perf() with LOGOCV to discriminate between reefs that are open or closed to fishing. Classification error rates (overall and balanced - BER) are represented on the y-axis with respect to the number of components on the x-axis for each prediction distance. Overall and balanced error rates show the same trend as the design is balanced (i.e. the same number of protected and non-protected reefs in each sampling trip). The plot shows that the error rate reaches a minimum with three dimensions with the centroids prediction distance. We therefore retained 3 PCs in downstream analysis.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}

megan_df <- data.frame(sample_data(megan_genus_clr), check.names = FALSE)

# Preserve the original row names by adding them as a column
megan_df$original_rowname <- rownames(megan_df)

# Adding the "Open_or_Closed_to_fishing" info now:
megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing <- left_join(megan_df, pMAGs_df, by = "REEF_NAME")

# Restore the original row names
rownames(megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing) <- megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing$original_rowname

# Remove the temporary column if desired
megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing <- megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing %>% 
  dplyr::select(-original_rowname)

# Verify row names are preserved
cat("Row names match:", identical(rownames(megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing), rownames(megan_df)), "\n")
head(rownames(megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing))

# Update the phyloseq object
sample_data(megan_genus_clr) <- megan_df_Open_or_Closed_to_fishing

### We can run MINT now:
read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector <- mint.splsda(X = read_based_OTUs,
                              Y = megan_genus_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing,
                              study = megan_genus_clr@sam_data$SECTOR_N_S,
                              ncomp = 10)
perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector <- perf(read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector)
plot(perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector)
```

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA error rate across sectors, fig.height=6, fig.width=8, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$global.error$BER
```

But it may also be interesting too see the stats on this within sectors - is the error higher in some sectors compared to the others?

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA error rates within sectors per study, fig.height=6, fig.width=8, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Initialize an empty list to store the results
study_errors_overall <- list()

# Loop through each study in the 'study.specific.error' section
for (study_name in names(perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector[["study.specific.error"]])) {
  # Extract the error rate for the current study
  study_error_overall <- perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$study.specific.error[[study_name]]$overall
  
  # Add the study name as a column to the error data
  study_error_with_name_overall <- cbind(Study = study_name, study_error_overall)
  
  # Store the error data in the list
  study_errors_overall[[study_name]] <- study_error_with_name_overall
}

# Combine all study data into a single data frame
study_error_df_overall <- do.call(rbind, study_errors_overall)

# Display the table
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(study_error_df_overall), caption = "MINT sPLS-DA - error rate (centroids distance) across GBR sectors")
```

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA error rate within sectors and separately for C and O, fig.height=6, fig.width=8, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Initialize an empty list to store the results
study_errors <- list()

# Loop through each study in the 'study.specific.error' section
for (study_name in names(perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector[["study.specific.error"]])) {
  # Extract the error rate for the current study
  study_error <- perf.read_based_mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$study.specific.error[[study_name]]$error.rate.class$centroids.dist
  
  # Add the study name as a column to the error data
  study_error_with_name <- cbind(Study = study_name, study_error)
  
  # Store the error data in the list
  study_errors[[study_name]] <- study_error_with_name
}

# Combine all study data into a single data frame
study_error_df <- do.call(rbind, study_errors)

# Display the table
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(study_error_df), caption = "MINT sPLS-DA - error rate (centroids distance) across GBR sectors, and separately for C and O")
```

### Tuning the number of features per dimension

We can choose the keepX parameter using the tune() function for a MINT object. The function performs LOGOCV for different values of test.keepX provided on each component, and no repeat argument is needed. Based on the mean classification error rate (overall error rate or BER) and a centroids distance, we output the optimal number of variables keepX to be included in the final model. This step was skipped and we retained 50 MAGs per each of the three dimensions.

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA open and closed in sectors tuning the number of features per PC, eval=FALSE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# But in case I ever decide to do the tuning, this would be the script
read_based_tune.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector <- tune(X = read_based_OTUs,
                                     Y = as.factor(megan_genus_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing),
                                     study = as.factor(megan_genus_clr@sam_data$SECTOR_N_S),
                                     ncomp = 5,
                                     test.keepX = seq(10, 500, 10),
                                     method = 'mint.splsda', #Specify the method
                                     measure = 'BER',
                                     dist = "mahalanobis.dist")
```

```{r read based plot MINT sPLS-DA features sector, fig.height=5, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Tuning plot of the MINT sPLS-DA models with up to 5 components. Diamonds represent the optimal number of features on a given component. Balanced error rate found on the vertical axis and is the metric to be minimised.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
plot(read_based_tune.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector, sd = FALSE)
```

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA features numeric sector, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
### Optimal nyumber of components
read_based_tune.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$choice.ncomp

### Optimal number of ffeatures per component
read.based.tune.mint.spls_da.optimal.keepX.sector <- read_based_tune.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector$choice.keepX # extract optimal values
read.based.tune.mint.spls_da.optimal.keepX.sector
```

```{r read based MINT PLS-DA sector protection status assessing the final model numerical outputs per class, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
read_based_tune.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector[["error.rate.class"]]
```

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA open closed final model sector, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
read_based.final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector <- mint.splsda(X = read_based_OTUs,
                                             Y = megan_genus_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing,
                                             keepX = read.based.tune.mint.spls_da.optimal.keepX.sector,
#                                             keepX = c(50, 50, 50), # Uncomment for arbitrary number of features
                                             study = megan_genus_clr@sam_data$SECTOR_N_S,
                                             ncomp = 2) # based on the BER
```

Symbols indicate the membership to an LTMP trip/transect. Component 1 discriminates between the two reef categories.", fig.height=6, fig.width=12, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}

Lastly, what about those spatiotemporal batch effects we observed in (s)PLS-DA?

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA sample plot open closed col per trip, fig.cap="Sample plot from the MINT sPLS-DA performed on the IMOS-MGD seawater MAGs to identify microbes that discriminate between reefs that are open or closed to fishing. Samples (reef sites) are projected into the MINT sPLS-DA space spanned by the first two components, and coloured by their corresponding category reflecting reef protection level. Symbols indicate the membership to an LTMP trip/transect. Component 1 discriminates between the two reef categories.", fig.height=5, fig.width=8, eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
plotIndiv(read_based.final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector,
          study = "global",
          comp = c(1,2), # We can look into comp 3 too, but I think 2 dimensions are enough
          legend = TRUE,
          group = sample_data(megan_genus_clr)$Sampling_trip,
          col =c("indianred", # Sampling trip 1
                "indianred4", # Sampling trip 2 
                "red3", # Sampling trip 3
                "slateblue"), # Sampling trip 4
          title = 'MINT sPLS-DA using IMOS GBR-MGD MAGs | PCs 1-2',
          subtitle = 'AIMS-LTMP trips', ellipse = T)
```

This plot shows that there is no longer clustering between the trips, suggesting we accounted for spatiotemporal batch effects.

### Correlation circle plot

We can examine our molecular signature selected with MINT sPLS-DA. The correlation circle plot highlights the contribution of each selected MAG to each component (close to the large circle), and their correlation (clusters of variables).

```{r read based MINT sPLS DA open.closed circle correlation plot sector, fig.height=13, fig.width=13, fig.cap="Correlation circle plot representing the MAGs selected by MINT sPLS-DA to discriminate between reefs that are open or closed to fishing, across the four sampling transects. We only show the MAGs selected by MINT sPLS-DA on components 1 and 2, and with a corr. cutoff = 0.8. This graphic should be interpreted in conjunction with the sample plot above - i.e. we observe a subset of seawater MAGs that are strongly correlated and positively associated to component 1 (positive values on the x-axis, on the right), which are likely to characterise the groups of reef sites that are open to fishing. We also observe a subset of seawater MAGs that are negatively associated to dimension 1 (x-axis, left) that may characterise reef sites that are protected/closed to fishing (and are negatively correlated to the previous group of MAGs).", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Exporting the names of taxa now, and making them short - easier plotting!
reads.name.super.short <- left_join(otu_table(megan_genus_clr) %>%
                              as.data.frame %>%
                              rownames_to_column("OTU"),
                            tax_table(megan_genus_clr) %>%
                              as.data.frame %>%
                              rownames_to_column("OTU")) %>%
  tidyr::unite(taxonomy, c(Family, Genus), sep = "; ") # Adding Taxonomy info
## Joining, by = "OTU"
reads.name.super.short <- as.character(reads.name.super.short$taxonomy)

# all gene names have the same first 10 characters, 
# shorten all the names to reduce visual clutter
plotVar(read_based.final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector,
        var.names = list(reads.name.super.short),
        cutoff = 0.7,
        )
```

### Loading plots

The plotLoadings() function displays the coefficient weight of each selected MAG in each IMOS GBR-MGD transect and shows the agreement of the molecular signatures across LTMP trips. Colours indicate the reef class (open or closed to fishing) in which the mean expression value of each selected MAG is maximal. These plots should be interpreted jointly with MINT sPLS-DA sample plots.

```{r read based Loading plots per sector, fig.height=30, fig.width=30, fig.cap="Loading plots of the MAGs selected by the MINT sPLS-DA on component 1 to discriminate between reefs that are open and closed to fishing, across sampling trips. Each plot represents one IMOS GBR-MGD transect, and the indicator MAGs are coloured according to the reef type (open or closed) they are maximally expressed in, on average. The length of the bars indicate the loading coefficient values that define the component. Several MAGs distinguish between reefs that are open or closed to fishing, and are consistently overexpressed in these samples across all sampling transects. The top 30 most influential/discriminant MAGs (on component 1) are shown.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
read_based_loading.plots.open.closed.per.sector <- plotLoadings(read_based.final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector,
             contrib = "max",
             method = 'mean',
             comp=1,
             legend = TRUE,
             legend.color = c("seagreen3", # Closed
                              "steelblue4"), # Open
#             ndisplay = 60,
             name.var = reads.name.super.short,
             study="all.partial",
             title="Contribution on comp 1",
#             subtitle = paste("Study",1:4)
             )
read_based_loading.plots.open.closed.per.sector
```

### Clustered Image Maps

The Clustered Image Map represents the enrichment levels of the MAG signature per sample. Here we use the default Euclidean distance and Complete linkage for the first component.

```{r read based Heatmap, fig.height=15, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Clustered Image Map of the MAGs selected by MINT sPLS-DA for component 1 only, to discriminate between reefs that are open or closed to fishing. A hierarchical clustering based on the MAG enrichment levels of the indicator MAGs on component 1, with reef sites in rows coloured according to protection level.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
read.based.cols.open.closed <- c("seagreen3","steelblue4")
read.based.open.closed.cols <- palette(read.based.cols.open.closed)[as.numeric(as.factor(megan_genus_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing))]

read.based.cols.open.closed <- c("seagreen3","steelblue4")
read.based.open.closed.cols <- palette(read.based.cols.open.closed)[as.numeric(as.factor(megan_genus_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing))]

# Exporting the names of taxa now, and making them short - easier plotting!
reads.name.short <- left_join(otu_table(megan_genus_clr) %>%
                              as.data.frame %>%
                              rownames_to_column("OTU"),
                            tax_table(megan_genus_clr) %>%
                              as.data.frame %>%
                              rownames_to_column("OTU")) %>%
  tidyr::unite(taxonomy, c(Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species), sep = "; ") # Adding Taxonomy info
## Joining, by = "OTU"
reads.name.short <- as.character(reads.name.short$taxonomy)

cim(read_based.final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector,
    comp = 1,
#    cutoff = 0.95,
    col.names = reads.name.short,
    margins=c(37, # bottom
              25), # right
    keysize = c(1, 0.4),
#    row.sideColors = color.mixo(as.numeric(as.factor(metadata_IMOS_MGD_MAGs$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing))),
    row.names = T,
legend = list(color.mixo(as.numeric(as.factor(megan_genus_clr@sam_data$Open_or_Closed_to_fishing))),
              title = "Reef protection level"),
    row.sideColors = read.based.open.closed.cols,
    title = "MINT sPLS-DA, component 1",
xlab = "Indicator MAGs that discriminate between take and no take zones",
ylab = "Reef sites")
```

### Performance of the MINT sPLS-DA model

Use of the auroc() function will yield a visualisation of classification performance when undergoing the LOGOCV procedure from above. The interpretation of this output may not be particularly insightful in relation to the performance evaluation of our methods, but can complement the statistical analysis. For example, the model's classification of open vs. closed sites had ~78% accuracy in classifying open and closed reefs in their corresponding category.

```{r read based MINT sPLS-DA model performance sectors, fig.height=4, fig.width=6, fig.cap="ROC curve and AUC from the MINT sPLS-DA performed on the IMOS GBR-MGD MAGs (876 MAGs, dereplicated in dRep at 95% ANI) for global component 1 for the open vs. closed reefs comparison. Numerical outputs include the AUC (0.7831) and a Wilcoxon test p−value (8.489e-12) for open vs. closed reefs class comparison that are performed per component.", eval=TRUE, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
read_based_MINT_sPLS_da_open_closed_model_performance.sectors <- auroc(read_based.final.mint.splsda.open.closed.sector,
                                                            roc.comp = 1,
                                                            print = FALSE)
read_based_MINT_sPLS_da_open_closed_model_performance.sectors$Comp1
```
